definition_zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的
definition_en: suitable and correct for a situation, belonging to one thing alone, or, in grammar, naming a particular person or place
core_image: 一件东西落进专为它留出的那个位置，不偏不倚，正正好好
scene: 正式晚宴前，主人把刀叉一件件摆正，餐巾折好放在盘子左侧。She checked that every guest had the proper glass beside the plate.
sceneCN: 这里取「适当的、合乎场合的」意思（第 1 个义项：适合当时场合与规矩的）；句意为她逐一确认每位客人的盘边都放着该配的那只酒杯。摆正刀叉的动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的

derivatives.zh: 由 proper 加 -ly 构成，义为「适当地；正确地」
由拉丁 proprietas 经法语进入英语，义为「财产；性质」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprietas，义为「得体；礼节」
在拉丁词干 propri- 前加 ad-，义为「合适的」

senses.title: Suitable and correct for the situation
senses.definition: right or suitable for a particular situation, purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某种场合、用途或某人来说正确或合适的
senses.example: Use the proper tool for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 干这活要用合适的工具。
senses.why: Latin proprius meant one's own, and what belongs to a thing is exactly what fits it, so the sense slid from belonging to being the right one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，而属于某物的东西恰恰就是适合它的东西，于是词义从「属于」滑到「正是该用的那一个」。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing alone
senses.definition: belonging by nature to one particular thing, person or group and not to any other
senses.definitionCN: 天然属于某一特定事物、人或群体，而不属于其他
senses.example: This bird is proper to the island and lives nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟是该岛特有的，别处见不到。
senses.why: The root sense of own is plainest here: a quality proper to something is a quality that belongs to it and to nothing else, which is why the word so often appears with to.
senses.whyCN: 「自己的」这层本义在这里最清楚：proper to 某物的性质，就是只属于它、不属于别处的性质，所以这个词常与 to 连用。

senses.title: Strictly so called
senses.definition: used after a noun to mean the central part of a place or thing, as opposed to the area around it
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指某地或某物的中心部分，以区别于其外围
senses.example: The market lies outside the old town proper.
senses.exampleCN: 市场位于老城区本身之外。
senses.why: If something is its own, the word can mark the thing itself as against its outskirts, and that is exactly how the after-noun use arose.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物是「它自己的」，这个词就能标出「事物本身」以区别于外围；后置用法正是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Naming one particular individual
senses.definition: in grammar, naming a particular person, place or thing rather than a whole class of them
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指称某个特定的人、地或物，而不是一整类
senses.example: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
senses.exampleCN: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。
senses.why: A proper noun belongs to a single bearer instead of a whole class, so the grammatical term preserves the old idea of exclusive ownership.
senses.whyCN: 专有名词只属于一个承担者而不属于一整类，所以这个语法术语保留的仍是「排他地拥有」这层旧义。

senses.title: Socially correct and respectable
senses.definition: behaving in the way polite society considers correct and respectable
senses.definitionCN: 按照讲究礼数的社会所认可、体面的方式行事
senses.example: It is not proper to ask about someone's salary.
senses.exampleCN: 打听别人的薪水不合规矩。
senses.why: A community decides what belongs to a well-run occasion, so propriety became a matter of manners and the adjective took on the sense of socially correct.
senses.whyCN: 一个共同体认定什么才属于「办得体面的场合」，于是 proper 也成了举止问题，形容词便带上「合乎社交规矩」的意思。

intro.en: Proper goes back to a Latin adjective meaning one's own, and every later sense is a variation on belonging.
intro.cn: proper 上溯到一个意为「自己的」的拉丁形容词，后来所有义项都是「归属」这一点的变奏。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, personal, not shared with others; a common but uncertain explanation derives it from pro privo, for a private person.
items.cn: proprius 意为自己的、个人的、不与他人共有的；一般认为它与 pro privo（为了私人）有关，但这一解释并不确定。

items.en: The noun proprietas named ownership and also the quality that belongs to a thing and makes it what it is.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 指所有权，也指属于某物、使该物成为其自身的性质。

items.en: Old French propre kept the senses of one's own, suitable and also clean or neat.
items.cn: 古法语 propre 保留了「自己的」「合适的」，以及「干净整洁的」这几层意思。

items.en: Middle English proper first meant belonging to someone or something, and older texts also use it for fine or excellent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 proper 最初指「属于某人或某物的」，较早的文本里还用它表示「出色的、优良的」。

items.en: Modern English settles on suitable, exclusive and strict, and keeps the old ownership in property, propriety, appropriate and the grammatical proper noun.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义定为「合适的、专属的、严格意义上的」，并把「归属」的旧义留在 property、propriety、appropriate 以及语法术语 proper noun 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for one's own; the near-meaning group gathers words about fitting and good manners.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「自己的」形容词上的词；近义组收关于「合适」与「礼节」的词。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from ownership and ends in fitness, and the whole family still turns on the question of what belongs where.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「归属」出发，走到「合宜」，整族词始终围绕「什么该在什么位置」这一问题。

normal.en: Latin proprius means one's own, so proper is about ownership before it is ever about manners.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，所以 proper 先说归属，之后才说礼节。

normal.en: Property and propriety share the same stem: what one owns, and what it is fitting to own or to do.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同一词干：一个是拥有的东西，一个是拥有或行事是否得体。

normal.en: The grammatical proper noun keeps the old sense, since such a name is owned by one person or one place.
normal.cn: 语法术语 proper noun 保留了旧义，因为这类名字只被一个人或一个地方拥有。

normal.en: After a noun, as in the city proper, the word marks the thing itself rather than the area around it.
normal.cn: 放在名词后，如 the city proper，这个词标出的是事物本身，而不是它周边的地带。

normal.en: Appropriate adds ad-, to, to the same stem: to make something one's own, and therefore to make it fit.
normal.cn: appropriate 在同一词干前加 ad-（向），意为「使成为自己的」，因此也就是「使之合宜」。

abstract.en: What is proper to a thing is what cannot be taken from it without changing what it is.
abstract.cn: 某物所专属的东西，一旦被拿走，它就不再是原来的它。

abstract.en: Manners and grammar seem far apart, yet both use proper to decide what belongs where.
abstract.cn: 礼节与语法看似相隔很远，却都用 proper 来判定什么该在什么位置。

abstract.en: A word for ownership became a word for correctness because fitting in has always been a matter of belonging.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有」的词变成了表示「正确」的词，因为「合宜」从来就是「归属」的另一面。

examples.en: Use the proper tool for the job.
examples.cn: 干这活要用合适的工具。

examples.en: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
examples.cn: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。

examples.cn: 市场位于老城区本身之外。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging, and the senses fan out from it: what fits because it belongs, what belongs to one thing only, the thing itself, a name owned by one bearer, and the manners a community expects.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「归属」，义项由它散开：因为属于所以合宜、只属于一物的特性、事物本身、只被一个对象拥有的名字，以及共同体期待的礼节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object dropping neatly into the one slot cut for it, with no gap on any side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西落进专为它挖出的那个凹槽，四边不留缝隙。

branches.cn: 客人挑对那把叉子

intro.en: A Latin adjective of ownership and the noun built from it hold the word together, and English suffixes turn the same stem into adverbs, nouns and related adjectives.
intro.cn: 表示归属的拉丁语形容词及由其构成的名词共同支撑这个词，英语后缀又把同一词干变成副词、名词和相关形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius, one's own, and the noun proprietas, ownership or peculiar quality, are the direct sources of the English word and of its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 proprius（自己的）与名词 proprietas（所有权、特性）是英语这个词及其同族词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地
definition_en: in the correct or suitable way; in a socially acceptable manner; (British, informal) completely or thoroughly
core_image: 工匠把一块木板量准、放平，直到它与墙面严丝合缝
scene: 木工把尺子贴紧墙边，反复对照图纸，确认每一块板都装在该在的位置。The carpenter checked the shelf twice to make sure it was properly fixed to the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 properly 是「正确地、恰当地」（第 1 个义项：以正确合适的方式）；句意为木匠检查了两次，确认搁板被牢牢固定在墙上。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、图纸、木搁板。

pos.zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到形容词，义为「恰当的；正确的；本身的」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprius（自己的），义为「得体的举止；合宜」
同出拉丁 proprius（属于自己的东西），义为「财产；房产；属性」
proper 前加否定前缀 im-，义为「不恰当的；不合规矩的」

senses.title: In the correct or suitable way
senses.definition: in the way that is correct, suitable, or expected for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 以正确、合适或符合某一用途所需的方式
senses.example: The machine will not work unless it is properly connected.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器如果没有正确接通，就无法运转。
senses.why: Properly is simply proper plus -ly, so it carries the old Latin sense of something sitting in its own place and fitting there exactly.
senses.whyCN: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，因此继承了拉丁语「待在自己位置、恰好贴合」的意思：装在该装的地方，才算正确地做。

senses.title: In a socially acceptable manner
senses.definition: in a way that follows good manners or accepted social standards
senses.definitionCN: 遵循良好礼节或公认社会标准的方式
senses.example: He was properly introduced to the guests before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚宴前，他被正式介绍给各位客人。
senses.why: If a thing belongs in its proper place, a person can also belong in the proper occasion, so the word slides from a fitted joint to fitted behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 东西有它该在的位置，人也有他该在场的场合，于是词义便从「装得对」滑向「举止合宜」。

senses.title: Completely; thoroughly (British, informal)
senses.titleCN: 彻底地；完全地（英式口语）
senses.definition: used in British informal speech to mean completely or very much
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中表示「完全地、非常」
senses.example: I was properly soaked by the time I got home.
senses.exampleCN: 等我到家时，已经浑身湿透了。
senses.why: When a job is done properly, nothing is left half-finished, so speakers began using the word for utterly or entirely, especially in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得 properly，就意味着没有一处半途而废；英式口语便借这层「做得彻底」引申出「完全地」。

senses.title: With good reason; justifiably
senses.definition: in a way that is fair, reasonable, or deserved
senses.definitionCN: 以公平、合理或应得的方式
senses.example: She was properly proud of the garden she had raised from seed.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是她从种子一手养大的，她理应为之自豪。
senses.why: Something proper is fitting, and what is fitting can also be deserved, which lets the word mark fair pride or fair blame rather than mere correctness.
senses.whyCN: proper 指「合宜」，而合宜的东西也就是应得的；于是这个词能标示理所应当的自豪或责备，而不只是「正确」。

intro.en: Properly is the adverb of proper, a word that reached English from Latin proprius by way of French, with -ly added to mark the manner of doing something.
intro.cn: properly 是 proper 的副词形式；proper 经法语来自拉丁语 proprius，加上 -ly 表示做事的方式。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, special, or belonging to a particular thing rather than to others.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、专属的」，指某物属于特定对象，而不属于别的对象。

items.en: The noun proprietas named the quality of belonging to someone, and it later split into English propriety and property.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 表示「归属某人的性质」，后来在英语中分化出 propriety 与 property。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as propre, meaning own, suitable, or clean, and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留形容词 propre，意为「自己的、合适的、干净的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English proper meant belonging to a person or thing and also fitting or correct, the sense that survives in proper behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语 proper 既指「属于某人或某物的」，也指「合适的、正确的」，后一义保留在 proper behaviour 中。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to proper, giving properly, which marks the manner of doing something in the right way.
items.cn: 英语在 proper 后加副词后缀 -ly 得到 properly，用来标示「以正确方式做某事」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem proprius; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for doing something the right way.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁词干 proprius 上的词；近义组收表示「以正确方式做事」的副词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from the Latin adjective proprius, its French descendant propre, and the ordinary English adverb ending -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁形容词 proprius、它的法语后裔 propre，以及最常见的英语副词后缀 -ly 组成。

normal.en: Properly is proper plus -ly, and -ly is the ordinary English ending for the manner of an action.
normal.cn: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，而 -ly 是英语里最常见的「做事方式」后缀。

normal.en: Something proper sits in its own place, so doing a job properly means putting every part where it belongs.
normal.cn: proper 的东西待在属于自己的位置，所以把事情做得 properly，就是把每个部分放到该放的地方。

normal.en: Improper is proper with the negative prefix im-, so improper behaviour is the exact opposite of proper behaviour.
normal.cn: improper 是 proper 前加否定前缀 im-，所以不得体的行为正是得体行为的反面。

normal.en: Property and propriety share one stem: one is what belongs to you, the other is what belongs to good manners.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同根：前者是归属于你的东西，后者是归属于良好礼节的东西。

normal.en: The phrase properly speaking marks the strict or exact use of a word, which is the correct sense of the adverb.
normal.cn: 短语 properly speaking 标示一个词的严格、准确用法，这正是这个副词「正确」的一面。

abstract.en: A joint that clicks into place is the whole idea of properly: no force left over, no gap left open.
abstract.cn: 一个卡进槽里的榫头就是 properly 的全部意象：用不上多余的力，也留不下一道缝。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a fitted shelf to a fitting remark, because both are judged by one question: does it belong here?
abstract.cn: 这个词可以从装好的搁板滑到一句合适的话，因为两者面对同一个判断：它属于这里吗？

abstract.en: When British speakers say properly soaked, they mean soaked through, which shows how correctness can slide into completeness.
abstract.cn: 英国人说 properly soaked 时意思是湿透，可见「正确」可以滑向「彻底」。

examples.en: The shelter must be properly anchored before the storm arrives.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，这个庇护所必须被妥善固定。

examples.en: She was properly dressed for the interview.
examples.cn: 她为面试穿得很得体。

examples.en: He was properly ashamed of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他对自己说过的话理当感到羞愧。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（自己的、专属的）→ 古法语 propre → 英语 proper；proper 加副词后缀 -ly 得 properly，义为「以正确、合宜的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is fitting into the right place; from there the word spreads to social manners, to complete thoroughness, and to what is deserved.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装进正确的位置」；义项由此扩展到社交礼节、彻底的完成，以及理所应得。

definition_en: something owned, especially land or buildings, or a quality that belongs to a thing

sceneCN: 这里指「归某人所有的财物与地产」，对应第 1 个义项：被拥有、可被继承的物；句意为清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏并注明归属。画面要点：地界石、主人的记号、并列的器物；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 财产；所有物；房产（不可数，指财物总体；表示一件件具体物品时可用复数）
性质；特性（可数，常用于科学语境，指某物固有的属性）

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

senses.title: Things that belong to someone
senses.definition: the things a person owns, taken as a whole, including goods, money and rights
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所拥有的东西的总和，包括货物、金钱与权利
senses.example: The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏，每件都注明属于某位继承人的财产。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'one's own', so the word begins as a label for whatever answers the question 'whose is it'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「自己的」，因此这个词起初就是给「这是谁的」这一问题的答案贴标签。

senses.title: Land and buildings
senses.definition: real estate, especially a house or plot that can be bought, sold or rented
senses.definitionCN: 不动产，尤指可买卖或出租的房屋或地块
senses.example: Property prices rose along the new railway.
senses.exampleCN: 新铁路沿线的房价上涨了。
senses.why: Land is the one thing that cannot be carried away, so it became the clearest test of who owns what.
senses.whyCN: 土地是唯一搬不走的东西，因此它成为「谁拥有什么」最清楚的检验。

senses.title: The right of ownership itself
senses.definition: the legal power to use, exclude others from, sell or give away a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物、排除他人、出售或赠予该物的法律权力
senses.example: Property is a bundle of rights, not merely the object held.
senses.exampleCN: 所有权是一束权利，而不只是手中所持之物。
senses.why: Lawyers separate the object from the right over it, and the word covers both, which is why one can own property in property.
senses.whyCN: 法学家把物与对物的权利分开，而这个词同时覆盖两者，所以人可以对财产享有财产权。

senses.title: A quality belonging to a thing
senses.definition: a characteristic that a substance or object has, such as colour, hardness or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 某物质或物体所具有的特征，如颜色、硬度或导电性
senses.example: The property that makes the alloy useful is its resistance to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 使这种合金有用的性质是它的耐热性。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing in the oldest sense includes not only goods but traits, because a trait is also something 'its own'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老意义上的「属于」不只包括财物，也包括特征，因为特征同样是某物「自己的」东西。

senses.title: Property in intangible things
senses.definition: ownership of ideas, marks, designs or other intangibles protected by law
senses.definitionCN: 对思想、标记、设计或其他受法律保护的无形之物的所有权
senses.example: A song can be property even though nothing physical is held.
senses.exampleCN: 一首歌可以是财产，尽管手中并未握着任何实体。
senses.why: If ownership is a legal relation rather than a physical grip, it can attach to what cannot be touched.
senses.whyCN: 如果所有权是一种法律关系而不是一把握持，它就能附着在摸不到的东西上。

senses.title: Objects used on a stage
senses.definition: the movable articles that an actor handles in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或影片中操作的可移动物件
senses.example: The props master checks every property before the curtain rises.
senses.exampleCN: 道具管理员在幕启前检查每一件道具。
senses.why: The theatre borrowed the legal word for 'things owned by the company', shortened it, and kept the sense of objects that belong to a production.
senses.whyCN: 剧院借用了「剧团所有的物件」这一法律说法，把它缩短，保留了「属于某场演出之物」的意思。

senses.title: An attribute in logic and mathematics
senses.definition: a feature that may be predicated of an object, or a rule that a mathematical structure satisfies
senses.definitionCN: 可以述说某一对象的特征，或某一数学结构所满足的规则
senses.example: The proof uses a property shared by all prime numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明用到所有素数共有的一个属性。
senses.why: The quality sense, pushed to its most abstract, becomes whatever can be said to belong to a class of objects.
senses.whyCN: 「性质」义被推到最抽象处，就成为一切可以说属于某类对象的特征。

senses.title: An estate or domain in older use
senses.definition: a landed estate with its house and lands, especially in historical and literary descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 连同宅邸与土地在内的地产，尤见于历史与文学描写
senses.example: The old property passed to the younger son.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧庄园传给了小儿子。
senses.why: Before land became a commodity it was an inherited domain, and that older meaning survives in descriptions of country estates.
senses.whyCN: 在土地成为商品之前，它是承袭而来的领地，这一较早的含义仍保留在对乡间地产的描写中。

intro.en: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership, quality', from proprius 'one's own'. The deeper origin of proprius is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been suggested but not settled. English took the word through Old French.
intro.cn: property 出自拉丁语 proprietas「所有权、性质」，源头为 proprius「自己的」。proprius 的更深来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但未成定论。英语经古法语吸收此词。

items.en: Proprius meant 'one's own, particular, not shared'; its own origin is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been proposed rather than proved.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、特有的、不共享的」；它本身的来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但这只是提出而非证实。

items.en: Proprietas named both ownership and the quality that belongs to a thing, so the two later English senses were present from the start.
items.cn: proprietas 同时指所有权与某物固有的性质，因此后来英语中的两个义项从一开始就已存在。

items.en: Old French proprete carried both senses into English, where the legal and material side soon became dominant.
items.cn: 古法语 proprete 把两个义项都带入英语，其中法律与财物的一面很快占据主导。

items.en: In Middle English the word could still mean a quality, but land, goods and the right over them increasingly answered to it.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个词仍可指性质，但土地、货物以及对它们的权利越来越多地用它来表达。

items.en: In modern usage the material sense dominates law and everyday speech, while the quality sense survives mainly in science and logic. The date of this separation is approximate.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，财物义主导法律与日常表达，而性质义主要保存在科学与逻辑中。这一分家的年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective for 'one's own' but has drifted into fitness, decorum and exclusivity; the second group gives near alternatives for belongings and for qualities.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个表示「自己的」拉丁形容词构成，但已漂向合适、得体与独占；第二组是「财物」与「性质」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: Correct or suitable, and in some phrases meaning 'itself'; the sense moved from 'belonging to a thing' to 'fitting that thing'.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，在某些短语中意为「本身」；语义由「属于某物」转为「合乎某物」。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour or of usage; it comes from the same source but describes what is fitting rather than what is owned.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或用语得体；它出自同一来源，但描述合乎礼仪之事，而不是被拥有之物。

entries.definition: Owned by a particular person or firm, or sold under an exclusive name; it is the adjective built on the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定个人或公司所有的，或以独占名称销售的；它是建立在所有权义上的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural means several pieces of real estate or several qualities; the theatre shortening props belongs here too.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式可指数处房产或数种性质；剧院用语中的缩略形式也归在这里。

entries.definition: The fact of having something in one's control; it can exist without legal ownership, which is why the two are distinguished in law.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于某人控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律上的所有权而存在，因此法律上把两者区分开。

entries.definition: Anything of value owned, seen from the balance sheet; it is a financial category rather than a legal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的任何有价值之物，从资产负债表的角度看；它是一个财务类别，而不是法律关系。

entries.definition: A large area of land with a house, or the total property a person leaves at death; it is narrower than the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 带有宅邸的大片土地，或某人去世时留下的全部财产；它比本词窄。

entries.definition: A characteristic regarded as belonging to a person or thing; it covers the quality sense of the entry word but never the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为属于某人或某物的特征；它覆盖本词的性质义，却从不覆盖所有权义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for 'one's own', real derived words and real legal phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词、真实派生词与真实法律用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Everything starts from the question 'whose is it', which is what 'one's own' answers.
normal.cn: 一切都从「这是谁的」这个问题开始，而「自己的」正是它的答案。

normal.en: The family runs proper, propriety, proprietor, proprietary and proprietorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括恰当的、得体、所有人、专有的与所有权。

normal.en: The same word covers the object and the right over it, so lawyers speak of property in property.
normal.cn: 同一个词既覆盖物，也覆盖对物的权利，因此法学家会说对财产享有财产权。

normal.en: Land is the clearest property because it cannot be carried away.
normal.cn: 土地是最清楚的财产，因为它搬不走。

normal.en: The theatre shortened the word to props, and the stage sense is still alive.
normal.cn: 剧院把这个词缩短为「道具」，舞台义至今仍活在使用中。

abstract.en: Picture a stone at the edge of a field with a name cut into it, and a chair, a cup and a coat laid beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象田野边缘一块刻着名字的石头，旁边摆着一把椅子、一只杯子和一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent box around an idea, marked with the same seal as the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明的盒子罩住一个想法，盒上盖着与房屋相同的印章。

abstract.en: Picture a substance whose label reads not 'mine' but 'this is what I am like'.
abstract.cn: 想象一种物质的标签上写的不是「我的」，而是「我本来就是这样」。

examples.en: The firm owns property in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市拥有房产。

examples.en: Hardness is a property that the alloy keeps at high temperature.
examples.cn: 硬度是这种合金在高温下仍保持的一种性质。

examples.en: The lease set out who was responsible for repairs to the property.
examples.cn: 租约列明了谁负责该房产的修缮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破坡地」——坡上那块地也是家产；再记住同一词还能指物之本性，就像地有坡、铁有硬。

root: 拉丁语 proprius「自己的、特有的」→ proprietas「所有权、性质」→ 经古法语 proprete 进入英语。proprius 的更深来源不确定，出自「为个体所有」短语的说法属假说；同根词包括 proper、propriety、proprietor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from what answers 'whose is it'. The owned things come first, with land and buildings as the clearest case; then the right of ownership itself, which can attach even to untouchable things; then the quality that belongs to a thing, at home in science and logic; and finally the stage objects and the older landed estate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「这是谁的」这一答案长出。先是被拥有的东西，其中土地与房屋最清楚；其次是对物享有所有权的权利，它甚至可以附着在摸不到的东西上；再其次是某物固有的性质，在科学与逻辑中安家；最后是舞台道具与较早的地产庄园义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone with a name on it, and the things inside the line that answer to that name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻着名字的地界石，以及界线之内属于这个名字的一切。

branches.en: THINGS: belongings in general, and the objects a theatre company owns for a production.
branches.cn: 物：一般意义上的财物，以及剧团为某场演出所拥有的物件。

branches.en: LAND: the immovable core, houses and plots that cannot be carried off.
branches.cn: 土地：不可移动的内核，搬不走的房屋与地块。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: ownership as a legal power, extending to intangibles such as songs and marks.
branches.cn: 权利：作为法律权力的所有权，可延伸到歌曲与标记等无形之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: what belongs to a thing's nature, in the laboratory and in logic.
branches.cn: 性质：属于某物本性的东西，在实验室里也在逻辑中。

branches.en: ESTATE: the older landed domain, inherited rather than traded.
branches.cn: 庄园：较早的领地，承袭而来而非买卖所得。

intro.en: One Latin adjective for 'one's own' supplies the whole family, with noun and agent endings added; the sense splits between what is owned and what a thing is like.
intro.cn: 一个表示「自己的」的拉丁形容词提供了整个家族，随后加上名词与施事后缀；语义在「被拥有之物」与「某物像什么」之间分开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及作名词用的中性形式。

items.example: The property passed to the eldest child.
The two properties share a fence.
items.exampleCN: 这两处房产共用一道篱笆。

items.example: That is the proper way to fold the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 那才是折这块布的正确方法。

items.example: The machine must be properly sealed.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器必须妥善密封。

items.example: The guests observed the proprieties of the house.
items.exampleCN: 客人们遵守这户人家的礼节。

items.meaning: the owner of a business or estate
items.example: The proprietor greeted us at the door.
The software is proprietary and cannot be copied.
items.exampleCN: 该软件为专有软件，不得复制。

items.example: The business is under sole proprietorship.

items.meaning: to take as one's own; suitable
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 议会拨出款项用于这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: a thing of one's own; a characteristic

专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

definition_zh: 比例；部分；份额；均衡；相称；（数学）比例式；大小、规模
definition_en: the relation between parts, or between a part and the whole, in size, amount, or importance
core_image: 一块蛋糕被切成大小不同的几份，每一份与整块之间都有固定的比
scene: 建筑师在图纸上反复比较窗户与墙面。If the window is too large the wall looks light and unstable, so the proportion of glass to brick has to be judged by eye.
sceneCN: 这里 proportion 是「比例、相称」（第 2 个义项：各部之间在大小上的关系）；句意：窗太大墙面就显得轻浮不稳，所以玻璃与砖的比例只能靠眼睛来把握。图中可辨识物件：建筑立面图、窗户、墙面分区、比例尺、铅笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 比例；部分；份额；均衡；规模

derivatives.zh: 成比例的；相称的
按比例地
相称的；成比例的
不成比例的

senses.title: A part relative to the whole
senses.definition: a part considered in relation to the whole amount
senses.definitionCN: 相对于整体而言的一部分
senses.example: A large proportion of students commute.
senses.exampleCN: 很大比例的学生通勤。
senses.why: Latin proportio joins pro- 'according to' to portio 'share'. The word begins with shares: one part measured against the whole it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proportio 把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合。这个词始于份额：一部分相对于它所属的整体被衡量。

senses.title: The relation between parts
senses.definition: the comparative size or amount of two or more parts
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个部分在大小或数量上的对比关系
senses.example: The proportion of sugar to flour matters.
senses.exampleCN: 糖与面粉的比例很关键。
senses.why: Two parts can be compared without a whole: this is the relational core. Cooking, chemistry, and design all depend on the ratio between ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 两部分可以脱离整体比较：这是关系性的核心。烹饪、化学与设计都依赖配料之间的比率。

senses.title: Correct balance or harmony
senses.definition: the quality of parts fitting together well
senses.definitionCN: 各部分彼此协调得当的性质
senses.example: The room has a pleasing sense of proportion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间有种悦目的比例感。
senses.why: Aesthetics evaluates the relation: some ratios look right, others jar. Proportion becomes a judgment, not just a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 美学评估这种关系：某些比率看起来对，另一些则刺眼。proportion 于是成了判断，而不只是测量。

senses.title: An equal share (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a share allotted to each person
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：分给每个人的一份
senses.example: Each heir received a proportion of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 每位继承人分得遗产的一份。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the simple share: portio is a portion. The mathematical sense grew from comparing such shares.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是简单的份额：portio 就是一份。数学义从比较这些份额生长出来。

senses.title: An equation of ratios (mathematics)
senses.definition: a statement that two ratios are equal
senses.definitionCN: 两个比率相等的陈述
senses.example: Solve the proportion 3/4 = x/12.
senses.why: Mathematics formalizes the comparison: a proportion asserts an equality between two ratios. The word keeps its 'share' root even in algebra.
senses.whyCN: 数学把比较形式化：比例式断言两个比率的相等。即使在代数中，这个词仍保留“份额”词根。

senses.title: Direct or inverse proportion
senses.definition: a relationship in which one quantity changes at a fixed rate with another
senses.definitionCN: 一个量随另一个量按固定比率变化的关系
senses.example: Speed is in direct proportion to distance over time.
senses.exampleCN: 速度与距离除以时间成正比。
senses.why: Science uses proportion for lawful co-variation: as one rises, the other rises or falls by a fixed factor. The ratio becomes a law of nature.
senses.whyCN: 科学用 proportion 指有规律的共变：一个上升，另一个按固定倍数上升或下降。比率成了自然法则。

senses.title: Size or dimensions
senses.definition: the size or scale of something, especially its relative dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大小或尺度，尤指相对维度
senses.example: The sculpture has heroic proportions.
senses.exampleCN: 这座雕塑体量宏伟。
senses.why: Proportions in the plural name the measured dimensions of a body or building. The relation becomes the thing itself: a person of large proportions.
senses.whyCN: 复数 proportions 命名身体或建筑被量出的维度。关系变成了事物本身：a person of large proportions。

senses.title: Proportional representation
senses.definition: an electoral system in which seats are allotted in proportion to votes
senses.definitionCN: 按得票比例分配席位的选举制度
senses.example: The party favors proportional representation.
senses.exampleCN: 该党支持比例代表制。
senses.why: Politics applies the ratio to power: votes are shares, and seats should mirror them. The word becomes a principle of fairness.
senses.whyCN: 政治把比率用于权力：选票是份额，席位应映照它们。这个词成了一种公平原则。

senses.title: Analogy or relation (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a correspondence or analogy between things
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：事物之间的对应或类比关系
senses.example: The proportion between microcosm and macrocosm was a medieval theme.
senses.exampleCN: 小宇宙与大宇宙的对应是中世纪的主题。
senses.why: Old philosophy used proportion for cosmic correspondences, not just numbers. The word could mean 'analogy', which is why proportionality once carried metaphysical weight.
senses.whyCN: 旧哲学用 proportion 指宇宙对应，而非只是数字。这个词曾可指“类比”，所以 proportional 一度带有形而上学分量。

intro.en: Proportion is a share word before it is a math word. Latin proportio joins pro- 'according to' with portio 'share', so it names the relation between allotments. Mathematics later made that relation exact.
intro.cn: proportion 先是份额词，然后才是数学词。拉丁语 proportio 把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合，因此它命名分配物之间的关系。数学后来把这种关系精确化。

items.en: First recorded as 'relation, correspondence, comparative share', from Latin proportio.
items.cn: 最早记录为“关系、对应、比较中的份额”，来自拉丁语 proportio。

items.en: proportio(nem) 'comparative relation, analogy' = pro- 'according to, for' + portio 'a share, a part'.
items.cn: proportio(nem)“比较关系、类比”= pro-“按照、为了”+ portio“份额、部分”。

items.en: portio 'a share' also gives portion, apportion, and proportion. The family is about dividing something into parts.
items.cn: portio“份额”还生成 portion、apportion、proportion。这个词族关乎把某物分成部分。

items.en: Here pro- does not mean 'forward' as in proceed or project; it means 'according to, in relation to'. The same prefix has several senses.
items.cn: 此处 pro- 不表示 proceed 或 project 中的“向前”，而表示“按照、相对于”。同一前缀有多种含义。

items.en: The mathematical and aesthetic senses become precise: proportion in geometry, and proportion in art and architecture.
items.cn: 数学与美学义变得精确：几何中的比例，以及艺术与建筑中的比例。

items.en: Modern English uses proportion for shares, ratios, balance, size, and electoral systems, all tracing back to portio.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proportion 指份额、比率、均衡、规模与选举制度，全部追溯到 portio。

note.en: The first group shares the portio stem; the second is about nouns that also mean a ratio or a share.
note.cn: 第一组共享 portio 词干，第二组看同样表示“比率”或“份额”的名词。

entries.definition: a share or piece of something. It is the simple noun behind proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 一份或一块。它是 proportion 背后的简单名词。

entries.definition: changing at a fixed ratio with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物按固定比率变化的。

entries.definition: to divide and distribute shares. It is ad- 'to' + portio.
entries.definitionCN: 分配份额。它是 ad-“向”+ portio。

entries.definition: the numerical relation between two quantities. It is the measured form of proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 两个数量之间的数值关系。它是 proportion 的测量形式。

entries.definition: a portion given to one person. It names the piece, not the relation between pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分给一个人的一份。它命名那块，而非块与块的关系。

entries.definition: an even distribution of parts or forces. It matches the aesthetic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 部分或力量的均衡分布。它对应美学义。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin portio 'share', pro- 'according to', the portion/apportion family, and the phrases in proportion to and out of proportion.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 portio“份额”、pro-“按照”、portion/apportion 词族，以及 in proportion to / out of proportion 两个短语。

normal.en: Portio means 'share'. Proportion is the relation between shares: this part against that part, or part against whole.
normal.cn: portio 意为“份额”。proportion 是份额之间的关系：这份对那份，或部分对整体。

normal.en: Here pro- means 'according to', not 'forward'. Proportion is measured according to the shares.
normal.cn: 此处 pro- 意为“按照”，不是“向前”。proportion 是按份额来衡量的。

normal.en: In proportion to means a fixed ratio holds; out of proportion means the ratio has broken, often in emotion.
normal.cn: in proportion to 意为固定比率成立；out of proportion 意为比率破裂，常用于情绪。

normal.en: A sense of proportion is a sense of relative size: knowing what matters how much.
normal.cn: a sense of proportion 是对相对大小的感觉：知道什么值多少。

normal.en: Proportional representation makes seats mirror votes: the political version of the same ratio.
normal.cn: 比例代表制让席位映照选票：同一比率在政治中的版本。

abstract.en: Proportion is how meaning is made from relation: nothing is large or small except against something else.
abstract.cn: 比例是从关系生成意义的方式：没有东西是大或小，除非相对他物。

abstract.en: A sense of proportion is a moral skill as much as an aesthetic one: it is knowing what deserves how much attention.
abstract.cn: 分寸感既是审美技能也是道德技能：知道什么该得到多少注意。

abstract.en: The word moves from shares to ratios to justice: fair distribution and exact measurement share one root.
abstract.cn: 这个词从份额走到比率再走到正义：公平分配与精确测量共享一个词根。

examples.en: The proportion of women in the workforce has risen.
examples.cn: 女性在劳动力中的比例上升了。

examples.en: Try to keep the problem in proportion.
examples.cn: 尽量把问题看得合乎分寸。

examples.en: The two quantities are in direct proportion.
examples.cn: 这两个量成正比。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若剖身”——把整体扑开、剖开身子分成几份 → proportion 比例、份额

root: 拉丁语 proportio“比较关系”，由 pro-“按照”+ portio“份额”构成；portio 还生成 portion、apportion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of proportion, all resting on a share. The share can be compared to the whole, to another share, to an ideal balance, to a mathematical law, to a body's size, or to a vote.
sensesIntro.cn: proportion 的九个义项都建立在“份额”上。这个份额可以相对整体、相对另一份、相对理想均衡、相对数学规律、相对身体大小，或相对选票。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: parts measured against one another and against the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：各部分彼此衡量，也与整体衡量。

branches.en: SHARE: one part set against the whole, or allotted to one person.
branches.cn: 份额：一部分相对整体，或分给一个人。

branches.en: RATIO: parts compared with each other, in arithmetic and in natural law.
branches.cn: 比率：部分彼此比较，在算术与自然法则中皆然。

branches.en: BALANCE: the relation judged as harmonious or fitting.
branches.cn: 均衡：这种关系被判断为和谐、得当。

branches.en: SIZE AND ANALOGY: measured dimensions, and the older idea of correspondence.
branches.cn: 大小与类比：被量出的维度，以及较早的对应观念。

branches.en: POLITICS: seats allotted in proportion to votes, making the ratio a rule of justice.
branches.cn: 政治：席位按选票比例分配，使比率成为正义规则。

intro.en: Proportion is a noun from Latin proportio. English adds -al, -ate, -ality, and the negative dis-, while portio also gives portion and apportion.
intro.cn: proportion 是来自拉丁 proportio 的名词。英语加 -al、-ate、-ality 与否定 dis-，portio 还生成 portion 与 apportion。

latinIntro.en: Latin proportio 'comparative relation' joins pro- 'according to' with portio 'share'. The portio family is about dividing into parts, which is why the word can mean both a ratio and a fair share.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proportio“比较关系”把 pro-“按照”与 portio“份额”结合。portio 词族关乎分成部分，所以这个词既能指比率，也能指公平份额。

definition_zh: 提议；建议；方案；求婚；投标
definition_en: a plan or suggestion offered formally for others to consider; also the act of suggesting, an offer of marriage, or a priced business bid
core_image: 一张写满条目的纸被推到桌子中央，等所有人点头
scene: 会议开到一半，负责预算的人把打印好的方案推到长桌中央，等各部门表态。The finance team submitted a detailed proposal for cutting costs by the end of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 proposal 是「提议、方案」（第 1 个义项：提交讨论的正式计划）；句意为财务团队提交了一份年底前削减成本的详细方案。图中可辨识物件：打印纸、长桌、预算表。

pos.zh: 提议；建议；方案；求婚

derivatives.zh: proposal 去掉后缀 -al 即得动词 propose，义为「提议；求婚」
propose 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -r，义为「提议者；提出者」
与 propose 同出拉丁 proponere，义为「命题；主张；提议」

senses.title: A formal plan put forward for others to consider
senses.definition: a plan or suggestion that is offered formally so that other people can discuss and decide on it
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出、供他人讨论并决定的计划或建议
senses.example: The committee will vote on the housing proposal next week.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会下周将对这份住房方案进行表决。
senses.why: Proposal is propose plus the noun ending -al, so it names the thing that has been placed before people and is waiting for their decision.
senses.whyCN: proposal 是 propose 加名词后缀 -al，因此它指「被摆到众人面前、正等他们决定」的那件东西。

senses.title: An offer of marriage
senses.definition: the act of asking someone to marry you
senses.definitionCN: 请求某人与自己结婚的行为
senses.example: Her answer to his proposal was a quiet yes.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他求婚的回答，是一声轻轻的愿意。
senses.why: A marriage proposal is also something laid before another person; only now the thing offered is a shared future instead of a plan.
senses.whyCN: 求婚同样是把东西摆到对方面前，只是这次献上的不是方案，而是一段共同的未来。

senses.title: The act of suggesting something
senses.definition: the act of putting an idea or suggestion to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或建议提交给某人或某群人的行为
senses.example: The proposal of new safety rules took the whole morning.
senses.exampleCN: 新安全规则的提出花了整整一上午。
senses.why: Because -al can name an action as well as its result, proposal can mean the offering itself, not only the document lying on the table.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -al 既能指动作也能指结果，proposal 便既能指「提出」这个动作本身，也能指桌上那份文件。

senses.title: A formal offer to do work or supply goods
senses.definition: a written offer from a company to do a job or supply goods at a stated price
senses.definitionCN: 公司按标价承接工程或供货的书面报价
senses.example: Three firms sent a proposal for the bridge repair.
senses.exampleCN: 有三家公司为桥梁维修提交了报价书。
senses.why: A business proposal places terms in front of a client, which is the same gesture of putting something forward, now with a price attached.
senses.whyCN: 商务提案是把条件摆到客户面前，与「把东西递上前」是同一个动作，只是这次附上了价格。

intro.en: Proposal is an English noun built from the verb propose and the suffix -al; the verb itself goes back to Latin pro- plus ponere, to place.
intro.cn: proposal 是英语里由动词 propose 加后缀 -al 构成的名词；动词本身可追溯到拉丁语 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or set down, and it supplies the core image of putting something in front of someone.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置、放下」，提供了「把东西摆到某人面前」这一核心意象。

items.en: Pro- meant forward, so proponere meant to put forward, to set before someone, or to offer.
items.cn: pro- 意为「向前」，所以 proponere 意为「摆到前面、呈现给某人、提出」。

items.en: Old French proposer took the Latin verb and meant to suggest or to set out, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 proposer 承袭了这个拉丁动词，意为「建议、陈述」，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: The noun ending -al was added to propose; the silent final e of the verb drops, so propos- plus -al gives proposal.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -al 加在 propose 上，动词末尾不发音的 e 脱落，于是 propos- 加 -al 就是 proposal。

items.en: Modern English uses proposal for plans, for offers of marriage and for priced business bids, while propose stays the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proposal 指方案、求婚与带价的商务报价，而动作仍由动词 propose 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for things offered for acceptance.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示「拿出供人接受之物」的名词。

entries.definition: To suggest a plan, or to ask someone to marry you.
entries.definitionCN: 提出计划，或向某人求婚。

entries.definition: A statement or idea offered for discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供讨论的陈述或主张。

entries.definition: The reason for which something is done; only the spelling looks similar, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的目的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An idea put forward for someone to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供人考虑的想法。

entries.definition: Something presented to someone for acceptance or refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 呈给某人、供其接受或拒绝的东西。

entries.definition: A formal suggestion made at a meeting for a vote.
entries.definitionCN: 会上提出供表决的正式动议。

entries.definition: A price offered for a job or at an auction.
entries.definitionCN: 为承接工程或在拍卖中出的价。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the verb propose with -al added, and the spelling drops the silent e before the suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是动词 propose 加 -al 而成，加后缀前先去掉不发音的 e。

normal.en: Proposal is propose with the noun ending -al, and the silent final e of propose is dropped before it.
normal.cn: proposal 是 propose 加名词后缀 -al，加之前 propose 末尾不发音的 e 脱落。

normal.en: The Latin verb behind both words is proponere, from pro- forward and ponere to place.
normal.cn: 这两个词背后的拉丁动词是 proponere，由 pro-（向前）与 ponere（放置）组成。

normal.en: A proposal is literally something placed forward, which is why it always faces a reader or a listener.
normal.cn: proposal 字面上就是「被摆到前面的东西」，所以它总是面对某个读者或听者。

normal.en: Marriage proposal uses the same noun because a shared future is also laid before the other person.
normal.cn: marriage proposal 用同一个名词，因为共同的未来也是被摆到对方面前的。

normal.en: Request for proposal is a fixed business phrase for asking firms to send their priced offers.
normal.cn: request for proposal 是固定的商务说法，用来请各公司寄出带价的方案。

abstract.en: The word is a hand pushing a sheet of paper across a table, and every sense keeps that gesture.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一只手把一张纸推过桌面，每个义项都保留着这个动作。

abstract.en: A plan, a marriage and a price are very different things, yet all three are offered by being set in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 方案、婚姻与价格是极不相同的东西，但三者都是靠「摆到对方面前」来献出的。

abstract.en: Because -al names both the act and its result, the same noun can mean the asking and the paper that carries it.
abstract.cn: -al 同时指动作和结果，所以同一个名词既能指「提出」这件事，也能指承载它的那张纸。

examples.en: The board will discuss the proposal tomorrow morning.
examples.cn: 董事会明天上午将讨论这份方案。

examples.en: He got down on one knee for his proposal.
examples.cn: 他单膝跪地求婚。

examples.en: Two suppliers sent a proposal with their prices.
examples.cn: 两家供应商寄来了附有报价的方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若剖搜」——把方案剖开、摆上桌面让人细看，记住 proposal 是提议。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）→ 拉丁 proponere → 古法语 proposer → 英语 propose；propose 加名词后缀 -al（末尾 e 脱落）得 proposal，字面义是「被摆到前面的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed in front of others; the senses divide into a plan, a marriage offer, the act of suggesting, and a priced bid.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被摆到他人面前的东西」；义项由此分为方案、求婚、提议这一动作，以及带价的投标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pushed to the middle of the table, waiting for heads to nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写好的纸被推到长桌中央，等着众人点头。

branches.en: a cost-cutting plan sliding across a long table
branches.cn: 一份削减成本的方案滑过长桌

branches.en: a ring held out on one knee
branches.cn: 单膝跪地时递出的戒指

branches.en: a chair asking the room to consider a new rule
branches.cn: 主持人请全场考虑一条新规则

branches.en: an envelope of prices arriving from three firms
branches.cn: 三家公司的报价信封先后送到

branches.en: one noun for a private question and a public one
branches.cn: 同一个名词，既指私人的一问，也指公开的提请

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin verb ponere, the prefix pro-, the French verb proposer, and the English noun ending -al.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁动词 ponere、前缀 pro-、法语动词 proposer，以及英语名词后缀 -al 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to suggest, to ask in marriage

definition_zh: 提议；建议；打算；求婚；提名
definition_en: to put forward a plan or idea for others to consider; to ask someone to marry you; to intend to do something; to nominate someone formally
core_image: 一只手把写着想法的纸推到桌面中央，抬头看向众人
scene: 小组讨论卡住时，最年轻的成员把一张草稿推到桌子中间，请大家先看他的思路。She proposed a shorter timetable so that the team could test the design earlier.
sceneCN: 这里 propose 是「提出、提议」（第 1 个义项：把计划或想法提出来供人考虑）；句意为她提出一个更短的时间表，好让团队更早测试设计。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、圆桌、马克杯。

pos.zh: 提议；建议；打算；求婚；提名

derivatives.zh: propose 加名词后缀 -al（末尾 e 脱落），义为「提议；方案；求婚」
propose 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -r，义为「提议者；提出者」
与 propose 同出拉丁 proponere，义为「命题；主张」
propose 的过去分词作形容词，义为「拟议中的；提议的」

senses.title: To put forward a plan or idea
senses.definition: to suggest a plan, idea, or course of action for other people to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出计划、想法或行动方案供他人考虑
senses.example: The engineer proposed a cheaper way to reinforce the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提出了一种更便宜的屋顶加固办法。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to place something in front of someone, so proposing is literally laying an idea on the table for others to look at.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「把东西摆到某人面前」，所以 propose 就是字面意义上的「把想法放到桌面上」让人看。

senses.title: To ask someone to marry you
senses.definition: to ask a person to marry you, usually in a formal or planned way
senses.definitionCN: 请求某人嫁给自己或娶自己，通常正式或经过安排
senses.example: He proposed to her beside the river where they first met.
senses.exampleCN: 他在两人初遇的河边向她求婚。
senses.why: An offer of marriage is placed before the other person like a plan, and the answer comes back as a decision in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 求婚也像一份方案那样摆到对方面前，对方的回答同样是一次决定。

senses.title: To intend or plan to do something (formal)
senses.definition: to intend to do something, especially as a stated plan
senses.definitionCN: 打算做某事，尤指作为已说明的计划
senses.example: The council proposes to close the lane to traffic on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会打算在周日封闭这条小路，禁止车辆通行。
senses.why: What is set before people as a plan also states what the speaker means to do, so the verb comes to mark intention.
senses.whyCN: 摆在众人面前的计划同时也表明了说话人打算做什么，于是这个动词便能标示「意图」。

senses.title: To nominate someone or put a motion formally
senses.definition: to name a person for a position, or to present a motion for a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 提名某人担任某职，或提出动议交付正式表决
senses.example: She was proposed as the next chair of the society.
senses.exampleCN: 有人提名她担任协会的下一任主席。
senses.why: A name can be placed before a group just as an idea can, so one verb covers nominating a person and moving a motion.
senses.whyCN: 名字和想法一样都能被摆到一群人面前，所以同一个动词既能指提名某人，也能指提出动议。

intro.en: Propose comes from Latin pro- forward and ponere to place, through the French verb proposer; the same stem with the noun ending -al gives proposal.
intro.cn: propose 来自拉丁语 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置），经法语动词 proposer 进入英语；同一个词干加上名词后缀 -al，就成了 proposal。

items.en: Ponere meant to place, set down, or fix in position, and it is the source of a large family of English words.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置、放下、固定在某处」，是英语中一大族词的来源。

items.en: With pro- meaning forward, proponere meant to put forward or set before someone, often as an offer.
items.cn: 加上表示「向前」的 pro-，proponere 意为「向前摆出、呈现给某人」，常带「献上」的意味。

items.en: Old French proposer carried the sense of suggesting or setting out, and English took the verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 proposer 带有「建议、陈述」的意思，英语在十四世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: Modern English propose covers plans, intentions, marriage and nominations, while proposal names the thing offered.
items.cn: 现代英语的 propose 覆盖计划、意图、求婚与提名，而 proposal 指被献出的那个东西。

items.en: Propose ends in a silent e, which drops before the noun ending -al, so propos- plus -al becomes proposal, never proposeal.
items.cn: propose 以不发音的 e 结尾，遇到名词后缀 -al 时这个 e 脱落，于是 propos- 加 -al 写作 proposal，而不会写成 proposeal。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and the Latin relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting an idea or a name forward.
note.cn: 形近组收这个动词的名词形式与拉丁同族词；近义组收「提出想法或名字」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a plan or a marriage offer that is put forward.
entries.definitionCN: 由「提出」而来的名词，指方案或求婚。

entries.definition: A statement or idea offered for discussion or proof.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供讨论或证明的陈述、主张。

entries.definition: To put forward an idea or theory for serious consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重提出某种想法或理论供人考虑。

entries.definition: The aim of an action; only the spelling looks alike, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的目的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To mention an idea for someone to think about.
entries.definitionCN: 提出一个想法供人考虑。

entries.definition: To advise that something is a good choice.
entries.definitionCN: 建议某事物是好选择。

entries.definition: To formally name someone for a position.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提名某人担任某职。

entries.definition: To have something in mind as a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 心里打算做某事。

normalIntro.en: The verb is built from pro- forward and ponere to place, and its noun keeps the same stem with -al instead of a final e.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词由 pro-（向前）与 ponere（放置）构成，它的名词用同一词干加 -al，而不用末尾的 e。

normal.en: Propose is pro- forward plus ponere to place: to place an idea before people.
normal.cn: propose 是 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置）：把想法摆到众人面前。

normal.en: Proposal is the same stem with -al, and the e of propose drops, so the noun is spelled propos-al.
normal.cn: proposal 是同一词干加 -al，propose 的 e 脱落，所以名词拼作 propos-al。

normal.en: Propose a toast and propose a plan use the same gesture of holding something out to others.
normal.cn: propose a toast 与 propose a plan 用的是同一个「把东西端给别人」的动作。

normal.en: Propose to someone keeps the offer image, with a shared life as the thing offered.
normal.cn: propose to someone 保留了「献上」的意象，只是献出的东西变成共同的生活。

normal.en: Propose a motion and propose a candidate both put a wording or a name in front of a group for a vote.
normal.cn: propose a motion 与 propose a candidate 都是把一段文字或一个名字摆到一群人面前等待表决。

abstract.en: The verb is an open hand: whatever it offers must be visible to the people who will decide.
abstract.cn: 这个动词就是一只摊开的手：它献出的东西必须让将要决定的人看得见。

abstract.en: A plan, a marriage and a name all travel the same path, from a private thought to a public table.
abstract.cn: 计划、婚姻与名字走的是同一条路：从私下的念头，到公开的桌面上。

abstract.en: The missing e in proposal is the trace of the verb handing its meaning over to the noun.
abstract.cn: proposal 里少掉的那个 e，正是动词把意义交给名词时留下的痕迹。

examples.en: The city proposed a new bike lane along the river.
examples.cn: 市里提议沿河修一条新的自行车道。

examples.en: He proposed to her after dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭后，他向她求婚。

examples.en: They propose to move the office closer to the station.
examples.cn: 他们打算把办公室搬到离车站更近的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若剖子」——把想法剖开摆到桌上，就是 propose，提议。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）→ proponere（摆到前面）→ 古法语 proposer → 英语 propose；去 e 加 -al 即得 proposal，两者同源，词义都围绕「把东西摆到人前」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is setting something before people; the senses divide into a plan, an offer of marriage, a stated intention, and a formal nomination.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「把东西摆到人前」；义项由此分为计划、婚姻的献出、已说明的意图，以及正式提名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a sheet of notes to the middle of the table and looking up at the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一张写满要点的纸推到桌子中央，抬头看向众人。

branches.en: a rough timetable pushed across a round table
branches.cn: 一张粗糙的时间表被推过圆桌

branches.en: a ring held out by the river at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时在河边递出的戒指

branches.en: a council paper stating what it means to do
branches.cn: 市政文件写明它打算做什么

branches.en: a name read aloud and seconded in a hall
branches.cn: 礼堂里念出一个名字并有人附议

branches.en: one verb for offering a plan and offering a life
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既献出方案，也献出一生

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin verb ponere, the prefix pro-, the French verb proposer, and the English nouns proposal and proposition.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁动词 ponere、前缀 pro-、法语动词 proposer，以及英语名词 proposal 与 proposition 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

senses.title: Criminal proceedings against an accused
senses.titleCN: 对被告的刑事起诉程序
senses.definition: the process of charging someone and pursuing the case in court
senses.definitionCN: 对某人提出指控并在法院推进案件的过程
senses.example: The prosecution began as soon as the evidence file reached the state's lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 证据卷一交到州律师手中，公诉程序就开始了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow forward, and the legal noun pictures the state following a charge through every stage of a trial.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前追随」，这个法律名词描绘的正是国家把一项指控追随到审判的每一个阶段。

senses.title: The prosecuting authority
senses.definition: the body or office that has the power to bring charges
senses.definitionCN: 有权提出刑事指控的机构或部门
senses.example: The prosecution decided not to pursue the minor charge.
senses.exampleCN: 检察机关决定不追究那项轻微的指控。
senses.why: An institution can stand for the act it performs, so the abstract noun also names the office that decides whether to charge.
senses.whyCN: 机构可以代表它所做的动作，所以这个抽象名词也指决定是否起诉的那个部门。

senses.title: The state's lawyers in court
senses.definition: the lawyers presenting the state's case in a particular trial
senses.definitionCN: 在具体审判中代表国家陈述案件的律师
senses.example: The prosecution sat on the left and the defence on the right.
senses.exampleCN: 控方坐在左边，辩方坐在右边。
senses.why: In courtroom speech the abstract noun becomes a collective label for the legal team on the charging side, like defence on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭用语里，这个抽象名词变成指控一侧律师团队的集体标签，正如另一侧被称为辩方。

senses.title: The decision to lay charges
senses.definition: the moment or act of formally charging a person
senses.definitionCN: 正式对某人提出指控的那一动作或时刻
senses.example: A prosecution at this stage would need stronger evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个阶段起诉，需要更有力的证据。
senses.why: The word covers the beginning as well as the whole case, because a charge is both a single decision and a long proceeding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既覆盖开端，也覆盖整个案件，因为一次指控既是一个决定，也是一段漫长的程序。

senses.title: Formal carrying out of a task
senses.titleCN: 正式从事、推行某项工作
senses.definition: in formal writing, the carrying out or pursuit of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中，指对某项活动的推行与从事
senses.example: He was praised for the prosecution of his duties during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 他因危机期间尽责履职而受到赞扬。
senses.why: The old sense of following something forward survives in formal prose, where any duty or study can be prosecuted, not only a crime.
senses.whyCN: 「把某事向前推进」的旧义在正式文字中保留下来：任何职责或研究都可以被「推行」，并不限于罪行。

senses.title: Pursuit or continuation of an undertaking
senses.titleCN: 事业或行动的继续推进
senses.definition: in older usage, the continued pursuit of a war, a policy or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，对战争、政策或计划的持续推进
senses.example: The history devotes a chapter to the prosecution of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这部史书用一章讲战争的进行。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to law, it named any energetic continuation, and military and political writing kept that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄到法律之前，它指任何有力的持续推进，军事与政治文字保留了这一较宽的范围。

senses.title: The evidence stage of a trial
senses.definition: the part of a trial in which the charging side presents its evidence
senses.definitionCN: 审判中由指控方出示证据的那一部分
senses.example: During the prosecution, three experts described the damaged wall.
senses.exampleCN: 在控方举证阶段，三位专家描述了受损的墙体。
senses.why: Since the state speaks first, its phase of the trial takes the name of the whole proceeding, a part standing for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 因为国家一方先发言，审判中属于它的那个阶段便取了整个程序的名字，以部分代整体。

senses.title: Pursuit of a claim in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中对请求的追究
senses.definition: in older legal writing, the pursuing of any claim or suit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早法律文字中，对任何请求或诉讼的追究
senses.example: The record notes the prosecution of a debt against the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记载了对该遗产的一笔债务追索。
senses.why: Civil claims were once prosecuted as well as criminal charges, and older documents use the noun for any claim pursued to judgment.
senses.whyCN: 民事请求一度与刑事指控一样被「追究」，较早文书便用这个名词指任何追究至判决的请求。

intro.en: Prosecution comes from Latin prosecutio, the noun of prosequi 'to follow forward', built from pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'to follow'. The oldest sense is continuation, and law narrowed it to the pursuit of a charge.
intro.cn: prosecution 来自拉丁 prosecutio，即 prosequi「向前追随」的名词，由 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成。最古老的含义是「继续」，法律把它收窄为对指控的追究。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow. It also stands behind sequence, consecutive and the second half of prosecute, showing how widely the idea of following spread.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。它也是 sequence、consecutive 以及 prosecute 后半的来源，可见「跟随」这一观念散布之广。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, to pursue, to continue'. In legal use it meant to pursue a charge or a claim.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。在法律用法中指追究一项指控或请求。

items.en: The noun prosecutio named the following or the pursuing, and could describe the continuation of any undertaking, not only a legal one.
items.cn: 名词 prosecutio 指追随或追究，可描述任何事业的继续，而不仅限于法律事务。

items.en: French legal usage applied the noun to the conduct of a case, and English borrowed it with that narrower focus already attached.
items.cn: 法语法律用法把这个名词用于案件进行，英语借入时已带着这一较窄的侧重。

items.en: English used prosecution for both the conduct of a criminal case and the carrying on of any business, keeping the two senses side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 英语用 prosecution 既指刑事案件的进行，也指任何事务的推行，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English centres the word on criminal proceedings, while the 'carrying out' sense survives in formal phrases about duties, studies or a war.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词的中心放在刑事程序上，而「推行」义保存在关于职责、研究或战争的正式说法里。

note.en: Group one separates the related verb and agent from a near look-alike with a hostile prefix and from a word that only shares spelling; group two sets the proceeding against the other names for a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根动词与施事者、一个带敌对前缀的形近词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；第二组把这个程序与案件的其他名目作对照。

entries.definition: To bring and conduct the case; prosecution is the proceeding as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起并推进案件；prosecution 指整个程序。

entries.definition: The lawyer who conducts the case; the prosecution can also mean the team or the proceeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指推进案件的律师；prosecution 也可指团队或程序。

entries.definition: Systematic mistreatment, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix makes it harassment, not litigation.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性迫害，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀使它成为迫害，而不是诉讼。

entries.definition: A ban or outlawry, from proscribere 'to write up publicly'; it shares the opening letters but not the following verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指禁令或剥夺公权，来自 proscribere「公开书写」；它与本词只共享开头字母，并不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a prosecutor or the conduct of a prosecution, not the proceeding itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与检察官或起诉行为有关的，不是程序本身。

entries.definition: The court hearing where evidence is tested; prosecution is the pursuing of the charge, which may end before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指检验证据的庭审；prosecution 指对指控的追究，可能在开庭前就结束。

entries.definition: The whole matter before a court, civil or criminal; prosecution belongs to the criminal side.
entries.definitionCN: 指提交法院的整个事项，民事刑事皆可；prosecution 属刑事一侧。

entries.definition: The formal steps of a legal action; prosecution is the state's pursuit of a charge within them.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律行动的一系列正式步骤；prosecution 是其中对指控的国家追究。

entries.definition: The formal accusation itself, often after a grand jury; prosecution is the process that follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指控文书本身，常在大陪审团之后；prosecution 是随后展开的程序。

entries.definition: A lawsuit in civil law or a military engagement; in legal speech it is broader and often civil.
entries.definitionCN: 指民事法中的诉讼，或军事行动；在法律用语中范围更广，且常指民事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real following verb, the real hostile prefix and the real procedural pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「跟随」动词、真实的敌对前缀，以及真实的程序配对。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: the state follows its charge from filing to verdict.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：国家把指控从立案一路跟到判决。

normal.en: Persecution has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': one follows to court, the other follows to harm.
normal.cn: persecution 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀意为「贯穿」：一个跟到法院，一个跟到伤害。

normal.en: Proscription is a look-alike about public writing, not about following.
normal.cn: proscription 是形近词，讲的是公开书写，而不是跟随。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: the prosecution and the defence, charging side and answering side.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：控方与辩方，指控一侧与答辩一侧。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

abstract.en: Picture evidence bags laid end to end, forming a path toward an empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象证据袋首尾相接，铺成一条通向空椅子的路。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a rope that the state keeps pulling, hand over hand, through every hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一根绳，国家一场庭审接一场庭审地双手交替往回拉。

abstract.en: Picture one side of a courtroom speaking first because the state is the one that complains.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭一侧先开口，因为提出申诉的是国家。

examples.en: The prosecution rested after four days of testimony.
examples.cn: 经过四天作证，控方结束了举证。

examples.en: Without the second witness, the prosecution would probably fail.
examples.cn: 若没有第二位证人，这场起诉很可能失败。

examples.en: He wrote a book on the prosecution of long wars.
examples.cn: 他写了一本关于长期战争如何进行的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究神」——把诉状层层剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的名词 prosecutio，由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成；古义为「继续、推行」，后收窄为「起诉」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal proceeding, through the authority, the courtroom team, the laying of charges, formal carrying out, the older continuation of an undertaking, the evidence stage, and the old pursuit of a claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事程序开始，经检察机关、庭上的控方团队、提起指控、正式推行工作、旧时对事业的继续、举证阶段，最后到旧时对请求的追究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence bags laid end to end toward an empty chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：证据袋首尾相接，铺向一把空椅子。

branches.en: THE PROCEEDING: the state follows its charge through every stage of court.
branches.cn: 程序：国家把指控追随到法院的每一个阶段。

branches.en: THE THREE FACES: the authority, the team in court and the single decision to charge are one system seen at different distances.
branches.cn: 三张面孔：检察机关、庭上团队与提出指控的那一个决定，是同一系统在不同距离下的样子。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any duty, study or war can be carried forward, which is what the verb meant before law took it over.
branches.cn: 旧义：任何职责、研究或战争都能被推行，这正是法律接管这个词之前它的意思。

branches.en: THE HEARING: the side that speaks first gives its name to the evidence stage.
branches.cn: 庭审：先发言的一侧把自己的名字给了举证阶段。

branches.en: THE WIDER CLAIM: older documents also prosecute debts and civil claims, not only crimes.
branches.cn: 更宽的请求：较早文书也「追究」债务与民事请求，并不限于罪行。

intro.en: Prosecution is a Latin action noun built on a verb of following, so it names a process rather than a person.
intro.cn: prosecution 是建立在「跟随」动词上的拉丁动作名词，所以它命名的是过程，而不是人。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'follow' gives prosequi; the participle prosecutus and the noun prosecutio supply the stem, and -tion makes the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成 prosequi；分词 prosecutus 与名词 prosecutio 提供词干，-tion 构成英语名词。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀给动作一个前进方向）
items.example: The prefix points the following forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」指向前方。
这个复合动词命名追究。

items.meaningCN: 已追究的（分词提供英语词干 prosecut-）
items.example: The participle supplied the English stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了英语词干。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程（名词后缀把动词转成程序名）
items.example: The suffix made a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成过程名词。

items.meaningCN: 对指控的追究（由动作转为整套程序）
推进案件的施事者（施事后缀把过程转成人）
