senses.title: The future in view: what lies ahead
senses.titleCN: 前景：前方等待的那幅图景
senses.definition: the possibility or expectation of something happening in the future, especially something good
senses.definitionCN: 对未来某事的可能性或预期，尤指好事
senses.example: The prospect of a long winter worried the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长冬季的前景让农民们忧心。
senses.why: The noun appears in the 1660s as 'expectation, ground of expectation', from the habit of looking forward. What the eye does in space, the mind does in time: it scans the horizon of coming events.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 17 世纪 60 年代出现，义为“预期、期待的依据”，来自“向前看”的动作。眼睛在空间里做的事，心智在时间里也做：它扫视将要发生之事的地平线。

senses.title: A chance that may come true
senses.titleCN: 可能性、机会：尚未兑现的那份可能
senses.definition: a chance or possibility that something will happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或成功的可能性
senses.example: There is little prospect of finding survivors after so long.
senses.exampleCN: 过了这么久，找到幸存者的可能性很小。
senses.why: The 1620s sense 'mental view or survey' let people speak of viewing a future outcome. Once an outcome is 'in view', it is a chance on the horizon rather than a certainty in hand.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代“心中的审视”这一义项，让人可以“看见”未来的结果。一个结果一旦“在视野里”，它就是地平线上的机会，而不是握在手里的确定。

senses.title: The sweep of the eye: a wide view
senses.titleCN: 景象、视野：眼睛扫过的那一大片
senses.definition: a view or scene, especially a wide one seen from a high place
senses.definitionCN: 景色、景象，尤指从高处看到的广阔视野
senses.example: From the hilltop we had a fine prospect of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 从山顶上，我们看到了山谷的美丽景色。
senses.why: From 1530s English, prospect meant 'extensive view of the landscape', straight from Latin prospectus 'distant view'. The word still carries the physical sweep of the eye before it carries hope.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 30 年代起，prospect 指“广阔的风景视野”，直接来自拉丁语 prospectus“远处的景色”。这个词先有眼睛的物理扫视，后才有希望之义。

senses.title: Someone worth watching: the promising person
senses.titleCN: 潜在客户、有前途的人选：值得盯住的那个人
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as likely to succeed, or a possible customer or candidate
senses.definitionCN: 被认为可能成功的人或事物；潜在客户或候选人
senses.example: The agent spends her mornings calling new prospects.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经纪人每天上午给新潜在客户打电话。
senses.why: From 1922, prospect named 'a person or thing considered promising', out of the 1660s sense of expectation of advantage. A good customer is someone in whom the seller sees a future.
senses.whyCN: 从 1922 年起，prospect 指“被认为有前途的人或事物”，源自 17 世纪 60 年代“预期好处”的义项。好客户，就是卖方在其身上看得见未来的人。

senses.title: Grounds for hoping
senses.titleCN: 预期的依据：凭什么盼着
senses.definition: grounds for expecting something; a reasonable basis for anticipation
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的预期依据；合理的盼望理由
senses.example: The deal offers no prospect of profit this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易今年没有获利的指望。
senses.why: The 1660s sense was not the hope itself but its ground: 'expectation, ground of expectation'. The landscape metaphor persists — a prospect is what the situation lets you see coming.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 60 年代的义项不是希望本身，而是希望的依据：“预期、期待的依据”。风景的隐喻仍在：prospect 就是局势允许你看见的、即将到来的东西。

senses.title: Looking for ore: to prospect the ground
senses.definition: to search an area for gold, oil, or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 在某地区寻找黄金、石油或其他矿藏
senses.example: They prospected the valley for copper throughout the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天他们都在那个山谷里勘探铜矿。
senses.why: The verb dates from 1841, from a specialized 1832 noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore'. The miner literally looks out over the land to see what it promises.
senses.whyCN: 动词始于 1841 年，来自 1832 年的名词专义“有矿苗的地方”。矿工字面上就是在土地上四处张望，看它许诺了什么。

senses.title: Surveying the site before building
senses.titleCN: 勘察、探测：动工之前先看一遍
senses.definition: to examine land or a site, especially to judge its potential or value
senses.definitionCN: 勘查土地或场地，尤指评估其潜力或价值
senses.example: Engineers prospected the site before the dam was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝获批之前，工程师们勘察了坝址。
senses.why: English had an older verb prospect 'look forth, look out over' (1550s) from Latin prospectare, a frequentative of prospicere. The mining sense revived that old surveying gesture.
senses.whyCN: 英语早有动词 prospect“向外看、俯瞰”（16 世纪 50 年代），来自拉丁语 prospectare，是 prospicere 的反复体。采矿义让这个古老的勘看动作重新流行。

senses.title: A mental survey: the wide view of a subject
senses.titleCN: 宏观审视：把一门学问摊开来看
senses.definition: a broad mental view or survey of a subject, situation, or period
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题、局势或时期的宏观心理审视
senses.example: The book gives a broad prospect of a century of science.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对百年科学史作了宏观的审视。
senses.why: The transferred sense 'mental view or survey' is recorded from the 1620s. The eye's sweep over a valley becomes the mind's sweep over a field of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: “心中的视野/审视”这一转移义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代。眼睛扫过山谷的动作，变成了心智扫过一片知识领域。

senses.title: The long straight avenue
senses.titleCN: 大街、大道：一眼望不到头的那条路
senses.definition: a wide, straight street or avenue, especially in a Russian city
senses.definitionCN: 宽阔笔直的大街或大道，尤指俄罗斯城市中的
senses.example: Nevsky Prospect runs straight through the heart of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 涅瓦大街笔直地穿过城市中心。
senses.why: In 1866 English borrowed Russian prospekt 'avenue', which itself came from Latin prospectus. A grand avenue is a street designed to give the eye a long, uninterrupted prospect.
senses.whyCN: 1866 年英语借入俄语 prospekt“大街”，而俄语这个词又来自拉丁语 prospectus。宏伟的大道，就是一条为了让视线获得漫长而不中断的前景而设计的街。

intro.en: Prospect is one of the spec- words: all of them are about looking. Latin prospicere 'look forward' gives the noun prospectus 'a distant view', and English extends the same word from landscape to expectation, to customers, and finally to mining.
intro.cn: prospect 是 spec- 词族的一员：它们都与“看”有关。拉丁语 prospicere“向前看”给出名词 prospectus“远处的景色”，英语再把同一个词从风景扩展到预期、客户，最后扩展到采矿。

items.en: Prospicere meant 'to look out on, look forward', built from pro 'forward' plus specere 'to look at'. Specere goes back to PIE *spek- 'to observe', a reconstruction with no written record, so that deepest layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: prospicere 意为“眺望、向前看”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成。specere 可追溯到印欧语 *spek-“观察”，但这是没有书面记录的重构，因此最深层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Prospectus, the past-participle stem used as a noun, meant 'distant view, look out; sight, faculty of sight'. It named both the thing seen and the power of seeing it.
items.cn: prospectus 由过去分词词干用作名词，意为“远处的景色、眺望；视觉、视力”。它既指被看见之物，也指看见的能力。

items.en: The noun enters English as 'the act of looking into the distance; the condition of facing something or a certain direction'. The looking is still literal.
items.cn: 名词进入英语时意为“向远处看的动作；朝向某物或某个方向的状态”。这里的“看”仍是字面义。

items.en: The meaning widens to 'an extensive view of the landscape' (1530s), then to 'mental view or survey' (1620s), then to 'that which is presented to the eye, a scene' (1630s).
items.cn: 词义先扩展为“广阔的风景视野”（16 世纪 30 年代），再扩展为“心中的审视”（17 世纪 20 年代），又扩展为“呈现于眼前之物、景象”（17 世纪 30 年代）。

items.en: 'Expectation, ground of expectation, especially of advantage' appears in the 1660s on the notion of looking forward. From it come 'person or thing considered promising' (1922) and the plural prospects, 'things looked forward to'.
items.cn: “预期、期待的依据，尤指好处”于 17 世纪 60 年代出现，基于“向前看”的意象。由此派生出“被认为有前途的人或事物”（1922）以及复数 prospects“所期待之事”。

items.en: Mining uses a specialized noun sense 'a spot giving prospects of ore' (1832), and the verb 'explore for gold or minerals' follows in 1841, from prospect (n.).
items.cn: 采矿业先有名词专义“有矿苗的地点”（1832），动词“勘探黄金或矿物”于 1841 年随后出现，来自名词 prospect。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spec- look or the -spect shape; the meaning group shares the idea of a future chance, but not its spelling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spec-“看”或 -spect 的外形；近义组共享“未来的机会”这一概念，但拼写不同。

entries.definition: a printed plan describing a school, company, or proposed enterprise. It is prospect plus the Latin noun ending -us.
entries.definitionCN: 介绍学校、公司或拟办事业的印刷章程。它就是 prospect 加上拉丁名词词尾 -us。

entries.definition: to look back at someone with esteem. It uses the same specere 'look' but with re- 'back'.
entries.definitionCN: 尊重；回头看某人并怀有敬意。它用同一个 specere“看”，但前缀是 re-“向后”。

entries.definition: a person who watches an event. The root is pure 'look', with no pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 观众；旁观者。词根是纯粹的“看”，没有 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: a way of seeing things from a particular point. It looks through a situation rather than forward.
entries.definitionCN: 视角；透视法。它是透过一个情境去看，而不是向前看。

entries.definition: the likely future of a situation. It is the closest everyday synonym of prospect in the sense of expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 前景；展望。在“预期”这一义项上，它是最接近 prospect 的日常同义词。

entries.definition: the chance that something will happen. It measures probability, while prospect often adds hope or dread.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；或然性。它衡量概率，而 prospect 常带有希望或忧虑的色彩。

entries.definition: a long, wide view, especially between rows of trees. It matches the landscape sense of prospect.
entries.definitionCN: 远景；狭长的视野，尤指树列之间的。它对应 prospect 的风景义。

entries.definition: the act of expecting something and preparing for it. It names the mental act that prospect describes as a view.
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期待。它命名的是 prospect 以“视野”来描绘的那种心理活动。

entries.definition: something that may exist or happen. It is neutral, where prospect usually implies evaluation.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性；可能之事。它是中性的，而 prospect 通常含有评价意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin specere 'to look', the spec- family, and the mining and customer senses that grew from the same gaze.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 specere“看”、spec- 词族，以及从同一道目光里长出的采矿义和客户义。

normal.en: prospect = pro- 'forward' + spect 'look': to look forward is to see a prospect.
normal.cn: prospect = pro-“向前”+ spect“看”：向前看，看见的就是前景。

normal.en: The spec- family is all eyes: spectator, inspect, respect, perspective, circumspect.
normal.cn: spec- 词族全是眼睛：spectator、inspect、respect、perspective、circumspect。

normal.en: A prospectus is the same word in a brochure: a school lets you look ahead at what it offers.
normal.cn: prospectus 就是同一个词做成的小册子：学校让你提前看见它能提供什么。

normal.en: A prospector looks over the ground exactly as you look over the future.
normal.cn: prospector（勘探者）打量土地的样子，正像你打量未来。

normal.en: Job prospects are literally 'things looked forward to' in the plural.
normal.cn: job prospects 字面上就是复数形式的“被向前看的事情”。

abstract.en: Future is treated as a landscape: you stand here and scan what is coming.
abstract.cn: 未来被当作一片风景：你站在此处，扫视将要到来的一切。

abstract.en: Looking and hoping are one gesture in this word; the eye and the mind share a horizon.
abstract.cn: 在这个词里，看与盼是同一个动作；眼睛和心智共享一条地平线。

abstract.en: The word travels from landscape to time to market: a view, a chance, a customer.
abstract.cn: 这个词从风景走到时间，再走到市场：一片景、一个机会、一位客户。

examples.en: The prospect of moving abroad excited her more than it frightened her.
examples.cn: 移居国外的前景让她兴奋多过害怕。

examples.en: Geologists spent three years prospecting for oil in the desert.
examples.cn: 地质学家在沙漠里花了三年勘探石油。

examples.en: The sales team treats every inquiry as a potential prospect.
examples.cn: 销售团队把每一次询价都当作潜在客户。

dict_mnemonic.text: pro（向前）+ spect（看）——向前看，前景就在眼前；谐音“普罗斯佩克特”：普查（pro）一遍，向前看矿藏 → prospect 前景；勘探

root: 源自拉丁语 prospicere“向前看、眺望”，由 pro“向前”加 specere“看”构成，名词 prospectus 意为“远处的景色”；核心是“向前看所得到的那片景”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one gaze. The eye first sweeps a landscape, then the mind sweeps the future; what is seen becomes a chance, a customer, a subject surveyed, a street, and finally ground to be searched for ore.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一道目光。眼睛先扫过风景，心智再扫过未来；被看见的东西依次变成机会、客户、被审视的学科、一条大街，最后成为要去地下搜寻矿藏的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing high and looking forward — the view ahead, in space or in time.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在高处向前看——空间或时间中前方的那片景。

chain: SEE A CHANCE IN A PERSON

branches.en: THE EXPECTED FUTURE: prospect as what is anticipated, and the grounds for that anticipation.
branches.cn: 被期待的未来：作为预期内容的前景，以及支撑这份预期的依据。

branches.en: THE CHANCE AND THE PERSON: a possibility on the horizon, and someone in whom a future is seen.
branches.cn: 机会与人：地平线上的可能性，以及被人看见未来的人。

branches.en: THE WIDE VIEW: the landscape before the eyes, and the broad survey before the mind.
branches.cn: 广阔视野：眼前的风景，以及心智对学科的宏观审视。

branches.en: LOOKING INTO THE EARTH: mining for ore, and surveying a site for what it may yield.
branches.cn: 向地下看：探矿，以及为评估潜力而勘察场地。

branches.en: THE LONG AVENUE: a street built to give the eye an unbroken prospect.
branches.cn: 长长的大道：一条为了让视线获得不中断前景而建的街。

intro.en: Prospect is pro- plus spec- plus -t. Its family shows the prefix pro-, re-, per-, circum- and in-, the root spec- 'look', and the noun and agent endings -tus, -tor, -ive and -ion.
intro.cn: prospect 是 pro- 加 spec- 再加 -t。它的词族展示前缀 pro-、re-、per-、circum-、in-，词根 spec-“看”，以及名词与施事后缀 -tus、-tor、-ive、-ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look at' is the base of spectator, inspect and respect; with prefixes it yields prospicere, respicere, perspicere and circumspicere, and the noun prospectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere“看”是 spectator、inspect、respect 的基础；加前缀又给出 prospicere、respicere、perspicere、circumspicere，以及名词 prospectus。

items.meaning: a view ahead; expectation; to search the ground
items.example: The prospect of promotion kept her working late.
items.exampleCN: 升职的前景让她一直工作到很晚。

items.example: Officials came to inspect the factory.
items.exampleCN: 官员们来检查这家工厂。

items.meaning: to look back at with esteem
items.example: Students respect a teacher who listens.
items.exampleCN: 学生尊敬愿意倾听的老师。

items.example: The stadium held fifty thousand spectators.
items.exampleCN: 体育场容纳了五万名观众。

items.meaning: a way of seeing through a scene
items.example: Travel gives you a new perspective on home.
items.exampleCN: 旅行让你对家乡有了新的视角。

items.meaning: to look out mentally; to guess or invest
items.example: Reporters speculated about the reason for her resignation.
items.exampleCN: 记者们推测她辞职的原因。

items.meaning: the side something presents to the eye
items.meaningCN: 方面；外观（看过去的那一面）
items.example: We discussed every aspect of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 我们讨论了计划的每个方面。

items.meaningCN: 谨慎的（四周看遍再行动）
items.example: She was circumspect in accepting the offer.
items.exampleCN: 她在接受这个提议时很谨慎。

items.meaning: looking inward at one's own mind
items.example: His diary is a record of quiet introspection.
items.exampleCN: 他的日记是一份安静内省的记录。

items.meaning: a printed plan that lets you look ahead
items.meaningCN: 章程；招股书（让人预先看清全貌）
items.example: The university's prospectus lists every course.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学的章程列出了每一门课程。

latinEntries.meaning: to look forward, look out on

definition_zh: 保护；防护；保障；为（文件等）设置保护
definition_en: to keep a person or thing safe from harm, damage or loss, whether by covering it, by guarding it in law and insurance, or by locking it behind a password
core_image: 一个人张开外套挡在孩子身前，雨点全落在那层布上
scene: 暴雨来得突然，母亲把外套撑开罩住孩子，自己的后背全湿了。She held her coat over the boy to protect him from the downpour.
sceneCN: 这里表示「保护、使不受伤害」（第 1 个义项：用身体或物件挡住危险）；句意为她把外套罩在男孩头上，替他挡住倾盆大雨。

pos.zh: 保护；防护；保障

collocations.phrase: protect a file with a password

derivatives.zh: 由 protect 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「保护；防护物」
由 protect 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「保护的；防护的」
由 protect 加表示施动者的 -or 构成，义为「保护者；保护装置」
由 protect 加否定前缀 un- 与过去分词词尾构成，义为「未受保护的」

senses.title: To keep someone safe from harm
senses.definition: to put a person or thing out of reach of harm or damage, usually by placing your body or an object between them and the threat
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物挡在伤害够不到的地方，通常以身体或物件横在人与威胁之间
senses.example: He raised his arm to protect the child from the flying glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他抬起手臂，替孩子挡住飞来的玻璃。
senses.why: Latin protegere joins pro-, in front, with tegere, to cover, so the first picture is a layer held on the side where the blow lands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 protegere 由 pro-（在前面）与 tegere（盖住）合成，最早的动作就是把一层遮盖挡在挨打的那一侧。

senses.title: To guard against a danger that cannot be touched
senses.definition: to take measures that stop disease, cold, rust or an attack from doing damage, even when the danger has no shape you can see
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施阻止疾病、寒冷、锈蚀或攻击造成损害，即使这种危险看不见形迹
senses.example: A thin film of oil protects the blade against rust.
senses.exampleCN: 薄薄一层油能防止刀身生锈。
senses.why: A cover works because anything reaching the surface is stopped there, so English moves the same verb from visible blows to frost, germs and rust, which also arrive from outside.
senses.whyCN: 遮盖之所以有效，是因为凡是够到表面的东西都被拦在那里；于是英语把这个动词从看得见的打击挪到霜冻、病菌和锈蚀上——它们同样来自外面。

senses.title: To secure a right or a possession by law or contract
senses.definition: to use laws, rules or insurance so that a person's rights, property or income cannot easily be taken away or lost
senses.definitionCN: 借助法律、规则或保险，使某人的权利、财产或收入不易被夺走或损失
senses.example: The new clause protects tenants from sudden eviction.
senses.exampleCN: 新条款保障租客不被突然赶走。
senses.why: Law and insurance do for a person's interests what a coat does for the body: they set an enforceable barrier in front of something valuable.
senses.whyCN: 法律与保险对人利益的用处，就跟外套对身体的用处一样：在贵重的东西前面立起一道能强制执行的屏障。

senses.title: To restrict who may open a file or device
senses.definition: to keep a file, account or device from being opened or changed by anyone who has not been allowed in
senses.definitionCN: 使文件、账户或设备不能被未获许可的人打开或改动
senses.example: She protected the folder with a password before lending the laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 把电脑借出去之前，她先用密码保护了那个文件夹。
senses.why: A password is the newest form of the same cover: it stands at the door of the file, and only those who know it may lift the cover.
senses.whyCN: 密码是这层遮盖最新的形态：它守在文件门口，只有知道它的人才被允许把遮盖掀开。

intro.en: Protect comes from a Latin verb that meant to cover something on its front side, and that covering later hardened into a legal and then a digital barrier.
intro.cn: protect 来自一个意为「在正面盖住」的拉丁动词；这层遮盖后来变硬，先成为法律屏障，再成为数字屏障。

items.en: Tegere meant to cover or to clothe, and it supplied the covering half of the word.
items.cn: tegere 意为覆盖、遮盖，是这个词里「盖住」的那一半。

items.en: Pro- put the covering in front, so protegere meant to hold something over a person and keep harm away.
items.cn: pro- 把遮盖物放到前面，于是 protegere 意为把某物罩在人身上，把伤害挡开。

items.en: The participle protectus described someone already sheltered, and English borrowed exactly this form rather than the plain verb.
items.cn: 分词 protectus 描述已经被遮护住的人，英语借的正是这个形式，而不是光秃秃的动词。

items.en: Protectio named the act of covering and defending, and through French it became the English noun protection.
items.cn: protectio 指遮盖与防卫的行为，经法语演变成英语名词 protection。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century and widened it from a physical cover to legal guarantees and finally to passwords.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个动词，把「物理遮盖」扩展到法律保障，最后又扩展到密码。

note.en: The first group is built on the Latin verb for covering, with one word that only shares the prefix and the opening letters; the second group gathers verbs for keeping something safe.
note.cn: 第一组建立在表示「遮盖」的拉丁动词上，其中一个词只共用前缀和开头几个字母；第二组收表示「使免受伤害」的动词。

entries.definition: Serving to keep someone or something safe from harm.
entries.definitionCN: 起保护作用的；防护的。

entries.definition: The act of uncovering something hidden, literally the removal of a cover.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏之物；字面义是「把盖子揭掉」。

entries.definition: A natural covering such as skin or a shell; a technical word that keeps the bare sense of covering.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤、外壳等天然覆盖物；专业用语，保留「覆盖」的本义。

entries.definition: A public expression of disagreement; it shares the prefix pro- and the first letters only, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表达反对；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To ward off an attack, often with force or with argument.
entries.definitionCN: 击退攻击，常靠武力或言辞。

entries.definition: To watch over someone or something in order to prevent danger.
entries.definitionCN: 看守某人某物以防范危险。

entries.definition: To put something solid between a person and a threat.
entries.definitionCN: 把实体挡在人与威胁之间。

entries.definition: To protect something important through careful rules or measures.
entries.definitionCN: 通过周密的规定或措施保护重要之物。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps one picture: a cover held on the side the blow comes from, whether the blow is rain, rust, a lawsuit or a stranger at a keyboard.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词始终保留一幅画面：遮盖挡在打击来的那一侧，不管打击是雨、锈、官司，还是键盘那端的陌生人。

normal.en: Pro- means in front and tegere means to cover, so protect is literally to cover something on its front.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前面」，tegere 意为「盖住」，所以 protect 字面上就是「在正面盖住」。

normal.en: Detect turns the picture around: de- takes the cover away, so to detect is to uncover what was hidden.
normal.cn: detect 把这幅画反过来：de- 把盖子拿走，所以 detect 是揭开被藏着的东西。

normal.en: Protection is the noun of the covering, protector is the person who holds it, and protective is the quality of being able to hold it.
normal.cn: protection 是这层遮盖的名词，protector 是举着它的人，protective 是能举得起它的性质。

normal.en: Unprotected adds un- to the participle, so an unprotected wire is simply a wire with no cover in front of it.
normal.cn: unprotected 在分词前加 un-，所以 unprotected wire 就是前面没有任何遮盖的电线。

normal.en: Protect looks like prove because both begin with pro-, but prove goes back to probare, to test, and has no cover in it at all.
normal.cn: protect 与 prove 都以 pro- 开头，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），里面根本没有「盖住」这层意思。

abstract.en: A cover only works while it stays on the side facing the danger, which is why protection is always directed outward.
abstract.cn: 遮盖只有留在朝向危险的那一侧才有效，所以保护总是指向外面。

abstract.en: One verb holds a child, a blade, a tenant and a file because all four can be harmed by something arriving from outside.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词能护住孩子、刀身、租客和文件，因为这四者都可能被从外面来的东西伤到。

abstract.en: To protect is to lend something of your own, a coat, a law or a password, to stand between another person and harm.
abstract.cn: 保护就是把自己的一件东西——外套、法律或密码——借出去，挡在别人与伤害之间。

examples.en: She held her coat over the boy to protect him from the downpour.
examples.cn: 她把外套罩在男孩头上，替他挡住倾盆大雨。

examples.en: These rules protect tenants from sudden eviction.
examples.cn: 这些规定保障租客不被突然赶走。

examples.en: The folder was protected with a password.
examples.cn: 那个文件夹已用密码保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑坦克」——读音近似「扑-坦克」，人扑过去挡在坦克前面，只为护住身后的人；记住 protect 是保护。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前面）+ tegere（盖、遮）→ protegere（在前面遮住、护住）→ protectus（被护住的），十五世纪进入英语。同族词 detect（de- 去掉 + tegere 盖，即揭开盖子）、tegument（覆盖物）都保留「盖」的画面。注意 protect 与 prove 都以 pro- 开头，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验、证实），两者只是前缀相同，词根完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a cover held on the front side; the senses spread from shielding a body to blocking invisible threats, to legal guarantees, and finally to a password at the door of a file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「挡在正面的那层遮盖」；义项从护住身体，扩展到拦住看不见的危险，再到法律保障，最后到文件门口的那道密码。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat spread wide in front of a child while the rain hits the fabric.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件外套在孩子身前撑开，雨点全打在那层布上。

branches.en: a coat held up against the rain
branches.cn: 外套撑起来挡雨

branches.en: oil spread thin over the blade
branches.cn: 薄油涂在刀身上

branches.en: a lease clause standing between a tenant and the street
branches.cn: 一纸租约条款挡在租客与街头之间

branches.en: a password box waiting at the folder door
branches.cn: 文件夹门口等着的密码框

branches.en: one word for a coat and for a law
branches.cn: 同一个词既指外套，也指法律

intro.en: A Latin verb of covering, a prefix that moves it to the front, and two English endings that make the noun and the adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示覆盖的拉丁动词、把它推到前面的前缀，以及造出名词与形容词的两个英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Tegere and protegere with their participles are the reliable Latin cognates, and the bare root teg- still shows in detect and tegument.
latinIntro.cn: tegere、protegere 及其分词是可靠的同源词；光秃秃的词根 teg- 至今还能在 detect 与 tegument 里看到。

items.meaning: to cover in front, to shield

definition_zh: 保护；防护；保护措施；保护区
definition_en: the state or act of being kept safe from harm, or a measure that keeps something safe
core_image: 一把撑开的伞把雨挡在头顶之外，伞骨下是一小片干的区域
scene: 举报人担心遭到报复，于是向监察机构求助。The new law offers protection for whistle-blowers who report waste.
sceneCN: 这里 protection 指「法律提供的保护措施」（第 2 个义项：由制度或规则提供的安全保障，使某人免受伤害或报复）；句意为新法律为举报浪费行为的吹哨人提供保护。图中可辨识物件：法律文本、举报信封、监察机构门牌、撑开的伞；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保护；防护；保护措施；保护区（可数或不可数）

senses.title: Physical shielding from harm
senses.definition: the state of being covered or guarded so that harm cannot reach
senses.definitionCN: 被覆盖或看守、使伤害无法到达的状态
senses.example: The umbrella offered little protection against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 那把伞对风几乎起不到防护作用。
senses.why: The Latin noun named a covering; the modern sense keeps that image of something placed between a person and a threat.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词命名一层遮盖；现代义保留「把某物置于人与威胁之间」的意象。

senses.title: Legal or institutional safeguard
senses.definition: a rule, law or arrangement that keeps a person or group safe from harm or retaliation
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或群体免受伤害或报复的规则、法律或安排
senses.example: The new law offers protection for whistle-blowers who report waste.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律为举报浪费行为的吹哨人提供保护。
senses.why: The law takes the place of the umbrella and stands between a person and a threat.
senses.whyCN: 法律替代雨伞，立在人与其威胁之间。

senses.title: Environmental conservation
senses.definition: measures taken to keep ecosystems, species or resources from damage
senses.definitionCN: 为防止生态系统、物种或资源受损而采取的措施
senses.example: The reserve was created for the protection of nesting turtles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个保护区是为保护筑巢海龟而设立的。
senses.why: Nature cannot hold an umbrella, so a reserve is built around it.
senses.whyCN: 自然无法自己撑伞，于是围绕它建立保护区。

senses.title: Social security against hardship
senses.definition: public arrangements that shield people from poverty, illness or unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 使人们免受贫困、疾病或失业的公共安排
senses.example: Social protection kept the family afloat after the layoff.
senses.exampleCN: 失业后，社会保障让这个家庭撑了下来。
senses.why: Hardship is a threat, so public arrangements are built as a cover.
senses.whyCN: 困境是一种威胁，于是公共安排被搭成遮盖。

senses.title: Safeguarding of personal data
senses.definition: rules and technical measures that keep personal information from misuse
senses.definitionCN: 防止个人信息被滥用的规则与技术措施
senses.example: Data protection requires consent before sharing.
senses.exampleCN: 数据保护要求在共享前取得同意。
senses.why: Information can be harmed, so rules form a layer around it.
senses.whyCN: 信息会受损，于是规则在它周围形成一层。

senses.title: Trade protection for domestic producers
senses.titleCN: 对本国生产者的贸易保护
senses.definition: tariffs or quotas that shield local industries from foreign competition
senses.definitionCN: 使本地产业免受外国竞争的关税或配额
senses.example: The minister argued for temporary protection of the steel sector.
senses.exampleCN: 部长主张对钢铁行业实行临时保护。
senses.why: A market under foreign competition is shielded like a town under attack.
senses.whyCN: 面对外国竞争的市场像受攻击的城镇一样被遮蔽。

senses.title: A protected area
senses.definition: a place legally set aside where wildlife or a site is shielded from development
senses.definitionCN: 依法划出、使野生动物或遗址免受开发的地方
senses.example: The reef is a marine protection where anchoring is banned.
senses.exampleCN: 这片珊瑚礁是一处禁止下锚的海洋保护区。
senses.why: When protection is fixed to a place, the abstract noun becomes a mapped area.
senses.whyCN: 当保护固定在某个地点，抽象名词就变成地图上的区域。

senses.title: Gear worn against injury
senses.definition: equipment worn to absorb impact or prevent injury in sport or work
senses.definitionCN: 在运动或工作中吸收冲击、防止受伤的装备
senses.example: Knee protection is compulsory on the course.
senses.exampleCN: 这条赛道上必须佩戴护膝。
senses.why: Padding is the umbrella worn on the body.
senses.whyCN: 护具是穿在身上的伞。

intro.en: Protection comes from Latin protectio 'a covering, defence', from protegere 'to cover in front', through French protection. The word is recorded in English from the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: protection 经法语 protection 来自拉丁 protectio「遮盖、防御」，后者出自 protegere「在前面遮盖」。英语自 14 世纪有记录。

items.en: Tegere 'to cover' gives the family its core image of a roof or shield over something.
items.cn: tegere「覆盖」给该词族提供核心意象：某物上方的屋顶或盾牌。

items.en: Protegere 'to cover in front, shield' added pro- 'before' to tegere.
items.cn: protegere「在前面遮盖、屏蔽」在 tegere 前加上 pro-「在前」。

items.en: Protectio named the covering or the act of shielding; its stem supplies protection and protector.
items.cn: protectio 命名遮盖或屏蔽行为；其词干提供 protection 与 protector。

items.en: Old French protection passed into English in the 1300s, first in legal and military contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 protection 于 14 世纪进入英语，最初用于法律与军事语境。

items.en: Environmental, data and social protection are nineteenth- and twentieth-century extensions of the legal sense.
items.cn: 环境、数据与社会保护是 19、20 世纪从法律义延伸出来的用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use is not precisely dated and the fourteenth-century figure is approximate. The Latin protegere and protectio layers are secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语使用没有精确年代，14 世纪之数为约数；拉丁 protegere 与 protectio 这两层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the noun from the verb, adjective and agent of the family; group two separates forms of safeguarding by scope.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与同族动词、形容词、施动者；第二组按范围区分各类保障。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a guarding quality; protection is the thing provided.
entries.definitionCN: 描述防护性质的形容词；protection 是被提供的东西。

entries.definition: One who or that which protects; protection is the state or measure, not the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指保护者或防护装置；protection 是状态或措施，不是施动者。

entries.definition: The action of shielding; protection is the resulting state or the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指屏蔽动作；protection 是结果状态或安排。

entries.definition: Specific safeguards, as in legal protections; the singular is usually the general state.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体保障措施，如法律保护条款；单数多为一般状态。

entries.definition: Resistance to a specific attack; protection is broader and includes prevention and care.
entries.definitionCN: 指对具体攻击的抵抗；protection 更宽，包含预防与照料。

entries.definition: The condition of being safe; protection is the measure that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指安全的状态；protection 是产生该状态的措施。

entries.definition: Careful management to prevent loss of natural or cultural resources; it is one form of protection.
entries.definitionCN: 指防止自然或文化资源流失的谨慎管理；是保护的一种形式。

entries.definition: Keeping a person in official care; protection can be legal without detention.
entries.definitionCN: 指由官方照管某人；protection 可以是法律性的而不涉及拘留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin noun of covering, the real family, and the collocations of law, environment and data.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「遮盖」名词、真实词族，以及法律、环境与数据领域的固定搭配。

normal.en: protegere 'cover in front' + -ion: the state of being covered.
normal.cn: protegere「在前面遮盖」+ -ion：被遮盖的状态。

normal.en: The family runs protect, protection, protective, protector, protectionism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protect、protection、protective、protector、protectionism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: environmental protection, data protection, legal protection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 environmental protection、data protection、legal protection。

normal.en: The noun is countable when it means specific measures.
normal.cn: 指具体措施时，这个名词可数。

normal.en: One umbrella covers rain, law, reefs and knees.
normal.cn: 一把伞同时覆盖雨、法律、珊瑚礁与膝盖。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella holding a dry circle open in a downpour.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞在暴雨中撑开一小片干燥的圆。

abstract.en: Picture a statute standing between a witness and a threat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条法规立在证人与威胁之间。

abstract.en: Picture a reef marked off by buoys so that no anchor can fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一片珊瑚礁被浮标圈起，任何锚都落不下去。

examples.en: The helmet gives reliable protection against a fall.
examples.cn: 头盔能在摔倒时提供可靠的保护。

examples.en: The park was declared a protection for the last wild herd.
examples.cn: 这座公园被宣布为最后一群野生兽群的保护区。

examples.en: Consumer protection laws require clear labelling.
examples.cn: 消费者保护法要求标示清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「protect（保护）+ -ion（状态）」——被护住的状态 → 保护；防护

root: 拉丁 pro-「在前」+ tegere「覆盖」→ protegere「在前面遮盖」→ protectio「遮盖、防御」→ 法语 protection → 英语 protection。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one umbrella: rain over a head, law over a witness, rules over a reef, welfare over a family, consent over data, a tariff over a mill, a reserve over turtles, and padding over a knee.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一把伞：替头顶挡雨、替证人挡法外报复、替珊瑚礁挡开发、替家庭挡困境、替数据挡滥用、替工厂挡竞争、替海龟挡侵扰、替膝盖挡冲击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open umbrella holding a small dry circle inside a downpour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把撑开的伞在暴雨中守住一小片干燥的圆。

branches.en: PHYSICAL COVER: umbrellas, helmets and padding take the blow.
branches.cn: 物理遮盖：伞、头盔与护具承受冲击。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL COVER: law, welfare and consent rules stand in for the umbrella.
branches.cn: 制度遮盖：法律、福利与同意规则替代雨伞。

branches.en: CONSERVATION: measures that keep ecosystems from damage.
branches.cn: 保护措施：防止生态系统受损的行动。

branches.en: TRADE COVER: tariffs shield producers from competition.
branches.cn: 贸易遮盖：关税使生产者免受竞争。

branches.en: PLACE: protection becomes a bounded area on a map.
branches.cn: 地点：保护变成地图上一块有边界的地方。

intro.en: Protection is a Latin action noun in -io built on the protegere stem; English adds further suffixes for agent, quality and doctrine.
intro.cn: protection 是由 protegere 词干加 -io 构成的拉丁动作名词；英语再加后缀表示施动者、性质与主义。

latinIntro.en: Latin protegere, protectio and tectus carry the covering image into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protegere、protectio 与 tectus 把「遮盖」意象带入英语。

items.example: Protection from the sun matters at noon.
The treaty made the state a protector.
items.exampleCN: 条约使该国成为保护者。

items.meaning: a policy of shielding domestic industry
items.exampleCN: 保护主义抬高国内价格。

items.meaning: one who favours such a policy
items.exampleCN: 那名保护主义者阻挠了条约。

items.example: Environmental protection is written into the charter.

items.exampleCN: 数据保护规则限制共享。

items.meaning: a legal order to keep someone safe
items.meaningCN: 保护某人安全的法院命令
items.example: A protection order was served that night.
items.exampleCN: 当晚送达了一份保护令。

definition_zh: 抗议；抗议活动；反对；申辩；坚称
definition_en: a public statement or action showing strong disagreement, the act of objecting in public, or a firm declaration that something is true
core_image: 一群人举着写满字的纸牌站在门前，谁都不肯散去
scene: 新规定贴出来的第二天清晨，居民们举着纸牌站到办公楼前，没有人愿意走开。Hundreds of residents gathered outside the office to protest against the new rule.
sceneCN: 这里表示「抗议、反对」（第 2 个义项：公开表达强烈反对）；句意为数百名居民聚在办公楼外，抗议这条新规定。

pos.zh: 抗议；抗议活动；异议
抗议；反对；申辩；坚称

derivatives.zh: 由 protest 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，义为「抗议者」
由拉丁词干 protestat- 加 -ion 构成，义为「声明；抗议」，语气正式
由 protesting 加 -ly 构成，义为「带着抗议地；不服地」

senses.title: A public expression of strong disagreement
senses.definition: a statement, gathering or march by which people show in public that they refuse to accept a decision or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 人们用声明、集会或游行的方式，公开表示不接受某项决定或某种状况
senses.example: The sit-in was a quiet protest against the closure of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 那次静坐是对关闭图书馆的一场无声抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to declare something publicly and call others to witness it; when the declaration is a refusal, the noun becomes the event in the street.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为公开声明并请人作证；当声明的内容是「不接受」时，名词就成了街头上的那场活动。

senses.title: To state in public that one objects
senses.definition: to say openly, often together with others, that something is wrong and ought to be changed
senses.definitionCN: 公开说出自己认为某事不对、应当改变，常与众人一起
senses.example: Villagers protested against the plan to dam the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民抗议在河上筑坝的计划。
senses.why: The same public declaration is now seen as an action rather than an event, so the verb keeps the crowd and the refusal but adds the doing.
senses.whyCN: 同一场公开声明被看成动作而不是事件，于是动词保留了人群与拒绝，只是多了一层「正在做」。

senses.title: To insist firmly that something is true
senses.definition: to say firmly that something is the case, especially when denying a charge or correcting what others believe
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地说某事就是这样，尤用于否认指控或纠正别人的看法
senses.example: He protested that he had never signed the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚称自己从未签过那份文件。
senses.why: Before it meant to object, the Latin verb simply meant to bear witness; that older layer survives whenever a person protests innocence rather than protesting a policy.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「反对」之前，这个拉丁动词只表示「作证」；一个人申辩自己无罪而不是抗议某项政策时，留下的正是那更早的一层。

intro.en: Protest goes back to a Latin verb for bearing witness in public; English first used it for a solemn declaration and only later for a refusal.
intro.cn: protest 可追到拉丁语中「公开作证」的动词；英语最初用它指郑重的声明，后来才用来指拒绝接受。

items.en: Testis meant a witness, the person who can stand up and say what happened.
items.cn: testis 意为证人，即那个能站出来说出发生了什么的人。

items.en: Testari meant to bear witness or to call someone as a witness, and it grew out of testis.
items.cn: testari 意为作证或请人作证，由 testis 派生而来。

items.en: With pro-, the witnessing moved into the open, so protestari meant to declare something publicly and solemnly.
items.cn: 加上 pro-，作证被推到公开场合，于是 protestari 意为公开而郑重地声明。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word as protest, a solemn declaration, and passed it into English around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语借入后写作 protest，意为郑重声明，约在十四世纪传入英语。

items.en: English kept the old sense of declaring, then added the modern one of objecting in public, and finally the quieter sense of insisting that one is right.
items.cn: 英语保留了「声明」的旧义，又添上「公开反对」的新义，最后还有「坚称自己没错」这层更安静的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin witness and the declaration built on it; the second group gathers words for objecting and for stating a grievance.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁语的「证人」及由此构成的「声明」；第二组收表示反对与诉说不满的词。

entries.definition: A formal declaration, especially one that objects to something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的声明，尤指表示反对的声明。

entries.definition: To give evidence as a witness, from the same Latin word for witness.
entries.definitionCN: 作为证人提供证词，出自同一个表示「证人」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A formal statement given by a witness in court.
entries.definitionCN: 证人在法庭上作出的正式陈述。

entries.definition: To keep someone safe; the prefix pro- is shared, but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 保护某人；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To say that you disagree with something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意某事。

entries.definition: To gather in public in order to show opposition or support.
entries.definitionCN: 公开聚集以表示反对或支持。

entries.definition: A statement that something is wrong, often made to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指出某事有问题的说法，常向当局提出。

entries.definition: A loud public expression of anger or disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 公众大声表达的愤怒或不满。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the Latin witness: someone stands up in the open and says what he or she will not accept or will not admit.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都留着那个拉丁语的「证人」：有人站到明处，说出自己不接受或不承认的事。

normal.en: Pro- means forth and testis means witness, so protest is to bring a witness's statement out into public.
normal.cn: pro- 意为向前、公开，testis 意为证人，所以 protest 就是把证人的话拿到公开场合说出来。

normal.en: Testify, testimony and protest all keep that witness, which is why a courtroom and a street march can share one root.
normal.cn: testify、testimony 与 protest 都保留着这个「证人」，所以法庭与街头游行能共用一个词根。

normal.en: The noun names the event and the verb names the doing, yet both need other people to hear the refusal.
normal.cn: 名词指那场活动，动词指正在做的动作，但两者都需要别人听见这份拒绝。

normal.en: Protesting that you are innocent keeps the oldest sense, because there the word is still a declaration rather than a complaint.
normal.cn: 申辩自己无罪保留的是最古老的那层意思，因为那里它仍是声明，而不是抱怨。

normal.en: The stress moves with the part of speech in British English, and that shift alone tells a listener whether the word is the event or the act.
normal.cn: 英式英语里重音随词性移动，单是这一变化就能让听者知道这个词指事件还是动作。

abstract.en: A protest asks to be heard before it asks to be obeyed, which is why it lives in the open air.
abstract.cn: 抗议先求被听见，才求被采纳，所以它总发生在露天的场所。

abstract.en: The same word covers refusal and declaration because both are a person standing up and saying what is true for them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指拒绝与声明，因为两者都是同一个人站出来，说出对他而言为真的事。

abstract.en: When a protest is ignored it tends to grow louder, while a declaration that is believed goes quiet, and one word holds both ends.
abstract.cn: 抗议被忽视时往往更响，声明被相信时反而安静，同一个词却装着这两端。

examples.en: Thousands joined the protest outside the town hall.
examples.cn: 数千人参加了市政厅外的抗议。

examples.en: They protested against the rise in bus fares.
examples.cn: 他们抗议公交车票价上涨。

examples.en: She protested that she had never met him.
examples.cn: 她坚称自己从未见过他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若泰斯特」——声音先「普」地一下炸开，再「泰斯特」地念出不满；记住 protest 是抗议、反对。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ testis（证人）→ testari（作证）→ protestari（公开声明、郑重宣称）→ 古法语 protest，约十四世纪进入英语。最早指「郑重声明」，后来才指「公开反对」。注意 protest 与 protect 只共用前缀 pro-：protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），protest 的词根是 testis（证人）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a public declaration; the senses divide into the event of objecting, the act of objecting, and the older sense of insisting on the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开声明」；义项由此分出作为事件的抗议、作为动作的反对，以及更古老的「坚称事实」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd holding signs in front of a door, saying aloud what they will not accept.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人举着纸牌站在门前，把不肯接受的事大声说出来。

branches.en: a row of signs lifted above a crowd
branches.cn: 人群上方举起的一排纸牌

branches.en: a chant rising outside a closed office
branches.cn: 紧闭的办公楼外响起整齐的喊声

branches.en: a man repeating that he never signed
branches.cn: 一个人反复说自己从未签过字

branches.en: one refusal spoken and acted at the same time
branches.cn: 同一份拒绝既被说出又被行动

branches.en: a word that objects and a word that swears
branches.cn: 一个既在反对又在申明的词

intro.en: A Latin noun for witness, a prefix that brings the statement into public, and the English endings that make the doer and the formal noun hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「证人」的拉丁名词、把声明带到公开场合的前缀，以及造出「人」与正式名词的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Testis, testari and protestari are the reliable Latin cognates; the same witness root also appears in testimony and testify.
latinIntro.cn: testis、testari 与 protestari 是可靠的同源词；同一个「证人」词根也出现在 testimony 与 testify 里。

definition_zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验；证明自己
definition_en: to show that something is true by evidence, to turn out to be a particular way, or to test something in practice
core_image: 一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停了下来
scene: 争论一直持续到深夜，直到有人把当年的登记簿翻到那一页，指着上面的签名。The old register proved that the land had belonged to her family.
sceneCN: 这里表示「证明、证实」（第 1 个义项：用证据使某件事确定为真）；句意为那本旧登记簿证明了这块地一直属于她家。

pos.zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验

derivatives.zh: 与 prove 同源的名词，经古法语 preove 而来，义为「证据；证明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被证实的；经考验的」
由 prove 加 -able 构成，义为「可证明的」
由 prove 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「证明……有误；驳倒」

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to give facts, documents or tests that make it certain that something is true or real
senses.definitionCN: 拿出事实、文件或检验，使某事被确定为真或确实存在
senses.example: The fingerprints proved that he had been in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹证明他曾在那间屋子里。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test something and find it good, so proving starts as an examination that ends in a verdict rather than as a mere opinion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验某物并认定它站得住，所以「证明」起初是一场检验，最后落成判决，而不只是看法。

senses.title: To turn out to be a particular thing
senses.definition: to be found, after events have unfolded, to have a certain quality, often one that was not expected
senses.definitionCN: 事情展开之后，被发现具有某种性质，且常是原先没料到的
senses.example: The shortcut proved longer than the road we usually take.
senses.exampleCN: 那条近路结果比我们常走的路还远。
senses.why: Once a test is finished, the result simply is what it is; English lets the verb carry that outcome, so a thing can prove difficult without anyone proving it.
senses.whyCN: 检验结束之后，结果就摆在那里；英语让这个动词直接承担结果，于是事物本身可以 prove difficult，而不需要谁去证明它。

senses.title: To test something in order to learn its quality
senses.definition: to try a method, a weapon or a machine under real conditions to see whether it works
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下试用某种方法、武器或机器，看它是否管用
senses.example: The engineers proved the new pump under heavy load before selling it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在重载下检验了新水泵，然后才出售。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer made visible: before a thing can be proved true, it has to be put to the test, and the verb still names that trial.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老那层意思的直接显现：在被证明为真之前，东西得先经受检验，而这个动词至今仍指那场试验。

senses.title: To show one's own ability or courage
senses.definition: to show through action that one deserves a place, a role or respect
senses.definitionCN: 通过行动表明自己配得上某个位置、角色或尊重
senses.example: She proved herself in her first month on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她在上夜班的第一个月就证明了自己。
senses.why: When the thing being proved is the speaker, the test and the result collapse into one act, which is why English says prove oneself rather than adding true as well.
senses.whyCN: 当被证明的对象是说话者本人时，检验与结果合成一个动作，所以英语说 prove oneself，不再额外加 true。

intro.en: Prove descends from a Latin verb that meant to test and to judge as good; English keeps both the trial and the verdict, and later let the word also mean to turn out.
intro.cn: prove 源自一个意为「检验并判定为好」的拉丁动词；英语同时保留了检验与判决，后来又让它表示「结果如何」。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest and of good quality, said of a person or a thing that had been checked.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、品质良好，用于经过查验的人或物。

items.en: Probare meant to test something and to approve it as good, joining the act of examining to the verdict.
items.cn: probare 意为检验某物并认可它合格，把查验的动作与判决连在一起。

items.en: The participle probatus described what had stood the test, and it is the shape behind the English word.
items.cn: 分词 probatus 描述经住了检验的东西，是英语这个词背后的形式。

items.en: Old French prover meant to test and to demonstrate, and it brought the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 prover 意为检验、论证，把这个动词带进英语。

items.en: English split the old family: proof became the noun for the evidence, while prove kept the testing and added the modern sense of turning out.
items.cn: 英语把这一族拆开：proof 成为表示证据的名词，prove 留住检验，又添上「结果是」这层现代用法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of testing, including the noun English split off from it; the second group gathers verbs for showing something to be true or false.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「检验」的拉丁动词，包括英语从它分出去的名词；第二组收表示「表明真假」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for evidence that settles a question, split off from the same French form.
entries.definitionCN: 能定下疑问的证据名词，与动词同出法语形式。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for something already shown to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 分词转作形容词，指已被证实的东西。

entries.definition: Likely to be true, from the same Latin verb of testing and approving.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的，出自同一个表示检验与认可的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To investigate closely, originally to test a wound or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查究，原指探查伤口或表面。

entries.definition: To show clearly by argument or by an example.
entries.definitionCN: 用论证或实例清楚地表明。

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实、准确。

entries.definition: To show that a fact is certain, often in a formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事实确凿，常较正式。

entries.definition: To be discovered to be a particular way in the end.
entries.definitionCN: 最终被发现是某种样子。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps the picture of a test that ends in a verdict: something is put under pressure, and the result is then allowed to speak.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词保留着「检验之后落成判决」的画面：某物被压上压力，然后让结果自己说话。

normal.en: Probare is to test and to approve, so prove carries a courtroom inside it: first the examination, then the finding.
normal.cn: probare 既是检验也是认可，所以 prove 里装着一间法庭：先审，再判。

normal.en: Proof is the same family seen as a thing rather than an act, which is why a proof is handed over while a prove is performed.
normal.cn: proof 是同一族词被看成「物」而不是「动作」，所以 proof 可以递过去，prove 只能被执行。

normal.en: Probable keeps the approving half: what is probable has enough testing behind it to be believed.
normal.cn: probable 保留了「认可」的那一半：很可能的事，背后已有足够的检验让人相信。

normal.en: Disprove adds dis- to the front, so the test now ends in rejection instead of approval.
normal.cn: disprove 在前面加 dis-，于是检验以否定而不是认可收场。

normal.en: Prove looks like protect because both start with pro-, but probare means to test, and there is no covering anywhere in it.
normal.cn: prove 与 protect 都以 pro- 开头，但 probare 意为检验，其中没有任何「遮盖」。

abstract.en: A proof is a test that has stopped being a question, and the verb marks the moment that change happens.
abstract.cn: 证据是一场不再提问的检验，而这个动词标出的正是那变化发生的瞬间。

abstract.en: One word covers testing, judging and turning out because all three are stages of the same examination.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指检验、判定与结果，因为三者是同一场查验的不同阶段。

abstract.en: To prove something is to accept that it might fail, which is why the word is as much about risk as about certainty.
abstract.cn: 证明某物，就是承认它有可能失败，所以这个词既关乎确定，也关乎冒险。

examples.en: The video proved that the door had been locked all night.
examples.cn: 录像证明那扇门整夜都锁着。

examples.en: The task proved harder than anyone expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务结果比任何人预料的都难。

examples.en: He worked two extra shifts to prove himself.
examples.cn: 他多上了两个班来证明自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普如夫」——像「扑过去捋清楚」，把乱糟糟的事捋到只剩一条真相；记住 prove 是证明。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直的、品质良好的）→ probare（检验、验后认可）→ probatus（经住检验的），经古法语 prover 进入英语；同族词还有 proof、probable、probe、probity。注意 prove 与 protect 都带前缀 pro-，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），两者只是前缀相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a test ending in a verdict; the senses run from proving a fact, through the result of events, to testing a thing and proving oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以检验收尾的判定」；义项从证明一个事实，到事情的结果，再到检验一物与证明自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of papers pushed across a table, and a stamp on the last page that ends every doubt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停下来。

branches.en: a register opened to the page with the signature
branches.cn: 登记簿翻到有签名的那一页

branches.en: a short cut that turns out longer
branches.cn: 结果反而更远的那条近路

branches.en: a pump running under heavy load
branches.cn: 重载下运转的水泵

branches.en: a new worker taking the hardest shift
branches.cn: 新人接下最难的班次

branches.en: one word for examining and for concluding
branches.cn: 同一个词既指查验也指结论

intro.en: A Latin adjective of good quality, the verb of testing built on it, and the French and English forms that split into proof and prove hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示品质良好的拉丁形容词、由它构成的「检验」动词，以及分化为 proof 与 prove 的法语、英语形式，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Probus, probare and probatus are the reliable Latin cognates, and proof is the same family seen as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: probus、probare 与 probatus 是可靠的同源词；proof 则是同一族词被看成名词的样子。

definition_zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；防备
definition_en: to give or supply something that is needed, to state a rule in a law or contract, or to support someone with money
core_image: 旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，再转身把干粮和水递给身后的人
scene: 洪水退去后的第三天，村口的空地上支起几张长桌，志愿者把水和面包摆成一排。The relief team came to provide blankets and hot food for the flooded villages.
sceneCN: 这里取「提供、供给」的意思（第 1 个义项：把别人需要的东西给出去）；句意为救援队来为受淹的村庄提供毛毯和热食。村口长桌上摆开的水和面包就是线索。

senses.title: To supply something that is needed
senses.definition: to give someone something they need or to make something available for use
senses.definitionCN: 把别人需要的东西给出去，或使某物可供使用
senses.example: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。
senses.why: Latin providere joins pro-, ahead, to videre, to see; seeing ahead means noticing a need before it arrives, and the next move is to get the thing ready and hand it over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 providere 把表示「在前」的 pro- 接在 videre（看）上：提前看见，就是在需求到来之前先察觉；察觉之后最自然的动作，就是把东西备好递过去，于是「预先看见」变成了「供给」。

senses.title: To state as a rule in a law or contract
senses.definition: to establish a rule or condition in a law, contract or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、合同或协议中确立某条规则或条件
senses.example: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。
senses.why: A rule written in advance is itself a kind of foresight: the text settles now what will happen later, so the verb that means to get ready also names what a document lays down beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 提前写好的条文本身就是一种预见：文本在此刻就决定了以后会发生什么，所以那个表示「预先备好」的动词，也用来指文件事先订下的内容。

senses.title: To support someone financially
senses.definition: to earn the money that allows another person, especially a family member, to live
senses.definitionCN: 挣钱供另一个人生活，尤指供养家庭成员
senses.example: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。
senses.why: Providing for someone is looking ahead on their behalf: the money is set aside before the need is felt, which is the household version of seeing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 供养一个人，就是替对方往前看：钱在需求出现之前就留出来，这正是「预先看见」在家庭里的样子。

senses.title: To make preparation against something
senses.definition: to take action in advance so that a possible problem or danger does less harm
senses.definitionCN: 提前采取行动，使可能出现的问题或危险危害更小
senses.example: They built the wall to provide against flooding in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修了这道墙，用来防备春季洪水。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is pure foresight with nothing given away: to provide against a risk is to see it coming and move before it lands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是纯粹的「预先看见」，与给东西无关：provide against 某个风险，就是看出它会来，并在它落地之前先动手。

intro.en: Provide is built from two Latin pieces meaning ahead and to see, and that single image of foresight later spreads into supply, legal rules and family support.
intro.cn: provide 由两个拉丁语成分构成，意思分别是「在前」和「看」；这一「预先看见」的画面后来扩展到供给、法律条文与养家。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it supplied the visual core of a large family of Latin words.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，为一大族拉丁词提供了「看」这个核心。

items.en: Pro- meant ahead or in front, so providere meant to see ahead, to foresee and to take care of something in advance.
items.cn: pro- 表示「在前、预先」，所以 providere 意为往前看、预见，并提前照管某事。

items.en: The noun providentia named foresight and careful management, and it survives in the English words providence and provident.
items.cn: 名词 providentia 指远见与谨慎的照料，它留在英语的 providence 与 provident 里。

items.en: Old French pourveoir kept both halves of the meaning: to foresee a need and to supply what it calls for.
items.cn: 古法语 pourveoir 保留了两半意思：既预见需求，也提供需求所需的东西。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as provide and carried the word into law, where a document provides, and into the household, where a wage provides for a family.
items.cn: 英语把拼写固定为 provide，并把这个词带进法律——文件可以「规定」，也带进家庭——工资可以「养家」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving what is needed.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示「给出所需之物」的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 为将来作准备的照管，常被归于更高的力量。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a look into the future, not with a gift, and its family keeps returning to foresight, readiness and the handover that follows.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是送礼；同族词反复回到预见、准备以及随之而来的交付。

normal.en: Pro- means ahead and videre means to see, so provide begins with a look into the future rather than with an object.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前」，videre 意为「看」，所以 provide 的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是某件东西。

normal.en: Provision is the noun built on the same stem: what has been seen ahead and therefore got ready.
normal.cn: provision 是同一词干上的名词：预先看见、因此备好的东西。

normal.en: The legal use, as in the law provides, works because a written rule also decides the future in advance.
normal.cn: 法律用法如 the law provides 之所以成立，是因为写下的规则同样在提前决定未来。

normal.en: Provider adds -er, the person who does the providing, exactly as in employer and adviser.
normal.cn: provider 加 -er，指做「提供」这件事的人，与 employer、adviser 的构造相同。

normal.en: Provided that keeps the past participle and turns it into a condition: if this is seen to, the rest follows.
normal.cn: provided that 保留过去分词形式，把它变成条件：只要这一点被照看到，其余便随之成立。

abstract.en: To provide is to act on a future you have already seen, which is why the word sounds like care more than charity.
abstract.cn: 提供是对一个你已经看见的未来采取行动，所以这个词听起来更像照料，而不像施舍。

abstract.en: A law that provides and a parent who provides are doing one thing: fixing tomorrow before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 法律规定与父母供养做的是同一件事：在明天到来之前就把它安排下来。

abstract.en: The whole word lives in the gap between seeing a need and meeting it.
abstract.cn: 从看见需求到满足需求之间的那段距离，正是这个词的全部所在。

examples.en: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
examples.cn: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。

examples.en: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.

senses.title: A condition written into a law or contract
senses.definition: a condition or clause in a law, contract or agreement that states what must be done
senses.definitionCN: 法律、合同或协议中写明必须如何做的条件或条款
senses.example: A provision in the lease forbids keeping pets.
senses.exampleCN: 租约中有一条条款禁止养宠物。
senses.why: Latin provisio meant a seeing ahead, and a clause is exactly foresight written down: the parties decide now what will happen if something goes wrong later.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provisio 意为「预先看见」，而条款正是被写下来的预见：各方在此刻就定好，以后出了某种情况该怎么办。

senses.title: The act of supplying something
senses.definition: the act of giving or supplying something, especially a service or a resource
senses.definitionCN: 给予或供应某物的行为，尤指服务或资源
senses.example: The provision of clean water is the city's first duty.
senses.exampleCN: 提供干净的饮用水是这座城市的首要职责。
senses.why: Once foresight turns into action, the action is supplying, and English uses the noun for the whole process of making something available.
senses.whyCN: 预见一旦化为行动，这个行动就是供应；英语用这个名词指「使某物可供使用」的整个过程。

senses.title: A store of supplies kept for future use
senses.definition: supplies of food, fuel or equipment kept ready, especially for a journey or an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 备好的食物、燃料或装备，尤指为旅途或应急准备的
senses.example: They laid in provisions before the snow closed the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在大雪封路之前备好了给养。
senses.why: What foresight produces is something set aside, so the noun shifts from the act of preparing to the goods sitting in the store room, usually in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 预见所产生的，就是被留出来的东西，于是这个名词从「准备的动作」转到「仓库里堆着的物资」，且常用复数。

senses.title: Preparation made in advance
senses.definition: arrangements made now so that a future need or risk is already taken care of
senses.definitionCN: 现在作出的安排，使将来的需求或风险已被照管到
senses.example: They made provision for their daughter's education years in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们多年前就为女儿的教育作了准备。
senses.why: This is the word at its closest to the Latin original: pure forethought, before anything has been handed over or stored.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最贴近拉丁原义的一层：纯粹的预先打算，还没有交出任何东西，也还没有囤起任何东西。

intro.en: Provision comes from a Latin noun of foresight built on the same verb as provide, and English borrowed the noun through French.
intro.cn: provision 来自一个表示「预见」的拉丁语名词，与 provide 建立在同一个动词上；英语是经法语借入这个名词的。

items.en: Videre meant to see, the plain visual root behind the whole family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，是整族词背后那个朴素的「看」的词根。

items.en: Providere meant to see ahead and to take care in advance, with pro- adding the forward direction.
items.cn: providere 意为往前看、提前照料，前缀 pro- 加上了「向前」的方向。

items.en: The noun provisio named the act of foreseeing and the care that followed from it; its stem provis- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 provisio 指预见这一动作以及随之而来的照料，英语保留的正是它的词干 provis-。

items.en: Old French provision carried the noun into the senses of supply and of a stipulated arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语 provision 把这个名词带到「供应」与「约定好的安排」这两层意思上。

items.en: Modern English uses the singular for a clause or the act of supplying, and the plural for goods stored up for a journey.
items.cn: 现代英语用单数指条款或供应的行为，用复数指为旅途囤起来的物资。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers words for clauses and for what is kept in store.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示条款与囤积之物的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is foresight that has cooled into an object, and its memories sit on the Latin stem, on the written clause and on the plural in the store room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是冷却成实物的预见，记忆点落在拉丁词干、写下的条款，以及仓库里的复数形式上。

normal.en: Provision and provide share the Latin verb providere, but the noun came through French while the verb came by another route, which is why the vowel changed.
normal.cn: provision 与 provide 共享拉丁语动词 providere，但名词经法语传来，动词走的是另一条路，所以元音变了。

normal.en: Provis- is the stem of Latin provisio, so the -sion ending was not added in English.
normal.cn: provis- 是拉丁语 provisio 的词干，所以 -sion 并不是英语后来加上的后缀。

normal.en: Provisional keeps the idea of something arranged in advance and adds the hint that the arrangement is only for now.
normal.cn: provisional 保留「事先安排」的意思，并加上「这个安排只管眼前」的意味。

normal.en: In contracts the word means a clause, because a clause is a piece of written foresight.
normal.cn: 在合同里这个词指条款，因为条款就是一段写下来的预见。

normal.en: The plural provisions almost always means food and equipment for a journey, not several clauses.
normal.cn: 复数 provisions 几乎总指旅途所需的食物和装备，而不是好几条条款。

abstract.en: Provision is foresight that has cooled into an object: a clause on paper or a sack in the store room.
abstract.cn: provision 是冷却成实物的预见：要么是纸上的一条条款，要么是仓库里的一袋粮食。

abstract.en: Every contract is a small machine for the future, and its provisions are the parts.
abstract.cn: 每份合同都是一台为未来造的小机器，条款就是它的零件。

abstract.en: To make provision is to admit that the future will ask for something you do not yet need.
abstract.cn: 作出准备，就是承认未来会来索要你此刻还不需要的东西。

senses.title: Belonging to the mind
senses.definition: relating to the mind and its processes of thought, feeling and perception
senses.definitionCN: 与心智及其思维、情感与知觉过程相关
senses.example: Sleep loss has both physical and psychological consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足既有生理后果，也有心理后果。
senses.why: Psyche meant 'breath, soul, mind'. Psychological marks whatever belongs to that inner life rather than to the body's machinery.
senses.whyCN: psychē 意为“气息、灵魂、心智”。psychological 标记属于这种内在生活、而非身体机制的东西。

senses.title: Of the discipline
senses.definition: belonging to psychology as an academic or clinical field
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学术或临床领域的心理学
senses.example: The paper appeared in a leading psychological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份顶尖心理学期刊上。
senses.why: Once psychology became a laboratory science in the 19th century, psychological came to mean 'of the discipline', covering experiments, journals and clinics.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪心理学成为实验室科学之后，psychological 开始指“属于该学科的”，涵盖实验、期刊与诊所。

senses.title: Working through feeling
senses.definition: affecting a person through emotions and mental state rather than physical force
senses.definitionCN: 通过情绪与心理状态而非物理力量影响人
senses.example: The threat of redundancy caused psychological harm long before any job was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员的威胁在任何岗位真正消失之前就已造成心理伤害。
senses.why: The word names effects that travel through the mind: fear, shame or anxiety can do damage even when no physical injury occurs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名经由心智传导的影响：恐惧、羞耻或焦虑即使没有身体伤害，也能造成损伤。

senses.title: Based on mental measurement
senses.definition: measured or assessed through mental tests and reported feelings rather than physical instruments
senses.definitionCN: 通过心理测试与自述感受而非物理仪器来测量或评估
senses.example: The trial used psychological scales to rate anxiety before and after treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 试验用心理量表评定治疗前后的焦虑程度。
senses.why: Research needed a word for data that comes from questionnaires and scales, so psychological marks the measuring method as well as the subject.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要为来自问卷与量表的数据找个词，于是 psychological 既标记研究对象，也标记测量方法。

senses.title: An edge in the mind
senses.definition: giving an advantage by affecting confidence, fear or motivation rather than resources
senses.definitionCN: 通过影响信心、恐惧或动机而非资源来取得优势
senses.example: Winning the first set gave the team a psychological advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 赢下第一盘给这支队伍带来了心理优势。
senses.why: Competition uses the adjective for edges that exist only in the mind: the score is level, but one side already feels beaten or emboldened.
senses.whyCN: 竞争用这个形容词指只存在于心里的优势：比分持平，但一方已感到被击败或受到鼓舞。

senses.title: Written from the inside
senses.definition: of a novel or film: focused on inner motives and feelings rather than external action
senses.definitionCN: 指小说或电影聚焦内心动机与感受，而非外部动作
senses.example: Critics praised the novel as a psychological study of grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说是对悲伤的心理研究。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the term for works that stay inside a character's mind, where plot matters less than motive.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借这个词指留在人物内心的作品，在这类作品中情节不如动机重要。

senses.title: The right moment for the mind
senses.definition: of a moment: judged to be the point when people are most ready to accept something
senses.definitionCN: 指被人判断为最易接受某事的时刻
senses.example: He waited for the psychological moment to raise the question of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 他等待心理上最合适的时机提出经费问题。
senses.why: The fixed phrase 'the psychological moment' treats timing as a mental condition: the instant when resistance is lowest and attention highest.
senses.whyCN: 固定说法“心理上的时机”把时机当作一种心理状态：阻力最低、注意最高的那一刻。

senses.title: Fought through the mind
senses.definition: of warfare or tactics: aimed at beliefs, morale and fear instead of physical targets
senses.definitionCN: 指针对信念、士气与恐惧而非物理目标的战争或战术
senses.example: Leaflets and broadcasts were part of a psychological campaign against the garrison.
senses.exampleCN: 传单与广播构成了针对守军的心理战的一部分。
senses.why: Military language uses the adjective when the target is morale: nothing is destroyed, yet the will to fight is attacked directly.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言在目标是士气时用这个形容词：没有东西被摧毁，但战斗意志被直接攻击。

intro.en: Psychological joins Greek psychē, 'breath, soul, mind', with logos, 'word, account, reason', through the Latin-formed psychologia. The -ical ending comes from Latin -icalis and Greek -ikos. The word began as a label for the study of the soul and ended up covering stress, novels, morale and warfare.
intro.cn: psychological 把希腊语 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”与 logos“言说、道理、理性”结合，经由拉丁形式的 psychologia 而来。-ical 词尾来自拉丁 -icalis 与希腊 -ikos。这个词最初是“研究灵魂”的标签，后来覆盖压力、小说、士气与战争。

items.en: Psyche meant 'breath, life, soul'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally connected with the idea of breathing, though no root is proved.
items.cn: psychē 意为“气息、生命、灵魂”。其更深来源不确定，一般认为与“呼吸”的观念有关，但没有被证实的词根。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'. Combined with other stems, -logia named a field of study or a body of discourse.
items.cn: logos 意为“言说、记述、理性”。与其他词干结合时，-logia 命名一个研究领域或一套论述。

items.en: The compound psychologia was coined in Latin by 16th-century scholars for the study of the soul, before any laboratory existed.
items.cn: 复合词 psychologia 由 16 世纪学者在拉丁语中造出，指对灵魂的研究，当时还没有任何实验室。

items.en: English formed psychological from psychology with the adjective suffix -ical, at first meaning 'of the soul or mind'.
items.cn: 英语用形容词后缀 -ical 从 psychology 造出 psychological，最初意为“属于灵魂或心智的”。

items.en: Wundt and others turned psychology into an experimental discipline, and psychological came to cover measurement, tests and clinical practice.
items.cn: 冯特等人把心理学变成实验学科，psychological 随之覆盖测量、测验与临床实践。

items.en: Psychological warfare was named in the two world wars, psychological novels flourished earlier in the century, and the adjective spread to stress, advantage and timing.
items.cn: 心理战在两次世界大战中得名，心理小说在 20 世纪初兴盛，这个形容词又扩散到压力、优势与时机。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from psychology, the adverb and the different-root physiological. The meaning group contrasts mental, emotional and cognitive descriptions.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与 psychology、副词，以及词根不同的 physiological；词义组比较 mental、emotional 与 cognitive 三类描述。

entries.definition: the study of the mind, or a person's mental make-up. It names the field, while psychological describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 对心智的研究，或某人的心理构成。它命名字科，而 psychological 描述属于该学科的东西。

entries.definition: in mental terms. It turns the adjective into a statement about how something affects the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 在心理层面上。它把形容词转为关于如何影响心智的陈述。

entries.definition: relating to the body's functions. It looks parallel but comes from physis 'nature' plus logos, a different stem from psyche.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体功能相关的。它看起来结构平行，却来自 physis“自然”加 logos，词干与 psychē 不同。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It comes from iatreia 'healing', not from logos 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗相关的。它来自 iatreia“治疗”，而非 logos“研究”。

entries.definition: relating to the mind. It is the plain everyday word and often pairs with health and illness, while psychological is more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智相关的。它是平实的日常词，常与健康、疾病搭配，而 psychological 更技术化。

entries.definition: relating to feelings. It covers one part of mental life, while psychological covers the whole inner system.
entries.definitionCN: 与情感相关的。它覆盖心理生活的一部分，而 psychological 覆盖整个内在系统。

entries.definition: relating to thinking, memory and perception. It names the intellectual side rather than feeling or morale.
entries.definitionCN: 与思维、记忆和知觉相关的。它指理智的一面，而非情绪或士气。

entries.definition: existing in a person's own experience. It marks the private side of what psychological studies measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于个人自身经验中的。它标记心理研究所测之物的私人一面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into psyche and logos, then let the inner-life picture cover stress, science, novels, advantage, timing and warfare.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 psyche 与 logos，再用内在生活的画面覆盖压力、科学、小说、优势、时机与战争。

normal.en: Split it as psyche + log + ical: mind + study + adjective. Psychological means 'of the study of the mind'.
normal.cn: 拆成 psyche + log + ical：心智、研究、形容词。psychological 意为“关于心智研究的”。

normal.en: Picture a head opened like a room, with feelings drifting around instead of gears.
normal.cn: 想象一个像房间一样打开的头，里面飘着情绪而不是齿轮。

normal.en: Physical harm hits the body; psychological harm hits the same person through fear and shame.
normal.cn: 物理伤害打身体；心理伤害通过恐惧与羞耻打同一个人。

normal.en: A psychological novel stays inside that room, watching motives instead of events.
normal.cn: 心理小说留在那个房间里，看动机而不是看事件。

normal.en: Psychological warfare attacks morale, so the target is that room rather than any building.
normal.cn: 心理战攻击士气，因此目标就是那个房间，而不是任何建筑。

abstract.en: Keep the two Greek halves visible: psyche is the subject, logos is the way of studying it.
abstract.cn: 让两个希腊部分保持可见：psychē 是对象，logos 是研究方式。

abstract.en: Notice that the adjective can describe both a science and a trick: the same word covers journals and warfare.
abstract.cn: 注意这个形容词既能描述科学也能描述手段：同一个词覆盖期刊与战争。

abstract.en: Contrast it with physiological: one studies the mind, the other the body, even though the words look like twins.
abstract.cn: 与 physiological 对照：一个研究心智，一个研究身体，尽管两词看起来像双胞胎。

examples.en: Researchers measured the psychological effects of isolation on long voyages.
examples.cn: 研究者测量了长期航行中隔离对心理的影响。

examples.en: The coach said the early goal gave his players a psychological lift.
examples.cn: 教练说那个早早的进球让球员们在心理上受到鼓舞。

examples.en: The museum mounted a psychological warfare exhibition from the cold war.
examples.cn: 博物馆举办了一场冷战心理战展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“赛可乐鸡扣”：赛场上喝口可乐，鸡血一扣，心理状态立刻不同。

root: 希腊 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”加 logos“言说、研究”构成 psychologia，加 -ical 为形容词；核心是“属于心智及其研究”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses point to the inner life: a mind that suffers, a science that studies it, an effect that travels through feeling, a scale that measures it, an advantage that lives in confidence, a novel that stays inside it, a moment when it is ready, and a war that attacks it directly.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向内在生活：会受苦的心智、研究它的科学、经由情绪传导的影响、测量它的量表、存在于信心中的优势、留在它内部的小说、它准备好的时刻，以及直接攻击它的战争。

core.en: The inner life of a person, and everything that acts on it or measures it.
core.cn: 一个人的内在生活，以及作用于它或测量它的一切。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the mind itself and the discipline that studies it.
branches.cn: 对象：心智本身以及研究它的学科。

branches.en: EFFECT: harm or advantage arrives through feeling, not force.
branches.cn: 影响：伤害或优势经由情绪而非力量到来。

branches.en: MEASURE: scales and tests turn inner states into data.
branches.cn: 测量：量表与测验把内在状态变成数据。

branches.en: FICTION: a narrative stays inside motive rather than action.
branches.cn: 虚构：叙事留在动机内部，而非外部动作。

branches.en: TIMING AND WAR: the mind is either ready to yield or actively attacked.
branches.cn: 时机与战争：心智要么准备好让步，要么正被主动攻击。

intro.en: Psychological is psyche plus logos plus the adjective suffix -ical. The items below follow the Greek stems into nouns, adverbs and neighbouring disciplines.
intro.cn: psychological 由 psyche、logos 与形容词后缀 -ical 构成。下列条目沿着这两个希腊词干走到名词、副词与邻近学科。

latinIntro.en: The Greek entries give the two stems. They explain why psychology, psychiatry and psychosomatic all begin with the same word for soul.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语条目给出两个词干，解释了为什么 psychology、psychiatry 与 psychosomatic 都以同一个表示“灵魂”的词开头。
