senses.title: The science of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心理学：研究心灵的那门科学
senses.definition: the scientific study of the mind and behavior
senses.definitionCN: 对心理与行为的科学研究
senses.example: She studied psychology to understand how memory works.
senses.exampleCN: 她学习心理学，以理解记忆如何运作。
senses.why: The word is recorded in the 1650s as 'the study of the soul', from Modern Latin psychologia, probably coined in Germany in the mid-16c. By 1748 it meant the science of mental phenomena; by the early 1890s, a behavioral science.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 17 世纪 50 年代记录为“对灵魂的研究”，来自新拉丁语 psychologia，很可能是 16 世纪中在德国造出的。到 1748 年它指“心理现象的科学”，到 19 世纪 90 年代初成为行为科学。

senses.title: The mind of a person: mental makeup
senses.titleCN: 心理、心理状态：一个人心里的那套构造
senses.definition: the mental and emotional makeup of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体的心理与情感构成
senses.example: The psychology of the crowd turned angry within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的心理在几分钟内变得愤怒。
senses.why: The name of the discipline slid over to its object. If psychology is the study of the mind, 'the psychology of X' is the mind of X — the thing studied rather than the study.
senses.whyCN: 学科名滑向了它的研究对象。如果 psychology 是研究心灵的学问，那么“X 的 psychology”就是 X 的心灵——是研究对象，而不是研究本身。

senses.title: Weapons of the mind: psychological warfare
senses.titleCN: 心理战：不动枪炮，先动人心
senses.definition: the use of propaganda, threats, or staged information to weaken an enemy's morale
senses.definitionCN: 利用宣传、威胁或安排好的信息削弱敌方士气
senses.example: The leaflets were pure psychology: they made the enemy doubt itself.
senses.exampleCN: 那些传单纯粹是心理战：它们让敌人开始怀疑自己。
senses.why: Psychological warfare is recorded in the early 20c.; in compounds and headlines the adjective is clipped, so psychology alone can name the campaign that attacks morale rather than bodies.
senses.whyCN: psychological warfare 记录于 20 世纪初；在复合词和标题里形容词常被省略，于是 psychology 本身就能指那场攻击士气而非身体的行动。

senses.title: A school of thought: one system among many
senses.titleCN: 心理学体系、学派：一家之言
senses.definition: a particular system or school of psychological theory
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定的心理学理论体系或学派
senses.example: Freudian psychology dominated the clinic for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 弗洛伊德心理学在诊所里主导了数十年。
senses.why: -logia means 'study of', but a named body of doctrine also takes the name: Jungian psychology, cognitive psychology. The discipline splits into psychologies, each with its own mind-model.
senses.whyCN: -logia 意为“对……的研究”，但一套有名字的学说也沿用这个名称：荣格心理学、认知心理学。学科分裂成多种 psychology，每一种都有自己的心灵模型。

senses.title: Reading people: practical psychology
senses.titleCN: 洞察人心：能当场用的那点心理学
senses.definition: a shrewd practical understanding of how people think, used to persuade or calm them
senses.definitionCN: 对他人如何思考的敏锐实际理解，用来说服或安抚他人
senses.example: The coach used a little psychology to settle the team before the final.
senses.exampleCN: 教练用了点心理策略，让球队在决赛前平静下来。
senses.why: When theory is applied in the moment, 'psychology' becomes a skill rather than a science: knowing which word will move a person. The abstract noun turns into a countable trick.
senses.whyCN: 当理论被当场应用时，psychology 就成了技能而非科学：知道哪个词能打动一个人。这个抽象名词于是变成了可数的小手段。

senses.title: The empirical science of behavior
senses.titleCN: 行为科学：从实验里长出的那门学问
senses.definition: the modern empirical science of behavior, especially since the 1890s
senses.definitionCN: 现代的经验性行为科学，尤指 19 世纪 90 年代以来
senses.example: Modern psychology relies on controlled experiments and statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 现代心理学依赖受控实验和统计。
senses.why: The behavioral-sciences sense is dated to the early 1890s. Laboratories replaced the armchair: the soul was no longer the object — measurable behavior was.
senses.whyCN: 行为科学义可追溯到 19 世纪 90 年代初。实验室取代了扶手椅：研究对象不再是灵魂，而是可测量的行为。

senses.title: The old study of the soul
senses.titleCN: 灵魂学：这个词最初的意思
senses.definition: the original 1650s sense: the study of the soul or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪 50 年代的本义：对灵魂或精神的研究
senses.example: Early psychology was closer to theology than to statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 早期心理学更接近神学，而不是统计学。
senses.why: Greek psykhē meant 'breath, spirit, soul', and -logia 'study of'. Before the mind was measured, it was the breath-like soul that the word set out to study.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 psykhē 意为“呼吸、精神、灵魂”，-logia 意为“研究”。在心智被测量之前，这个词要研究的是那口气息般的灵魂。

senses.title: The mind of a group: consumer and social psychology
senses.titleCN: 群体心理：一群人共享的那颗心
senses.definition: the mental processes of a group, market, or public considered as a subject of study
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个研究对象的群体、市场或公众的心理过程
senses.example: The psychology of consumers shapes every advertising campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者的心理塑造着每一场广告活动。
senses.why: 'The psychology of X' extends the discipline to any collective mind. Advertising, politics and sport all borrow the laboratory's name for the crowd's inner life.
senses.whyCN: “X 的 psychology”把学科扩展到任何集体心智。广告、政治和体育都借实验室的名字，来指人群的内心生活。

senses.title: Inner life in a story
senses.titleCN: 人物心理：小说里被写出来的内心
senses.definition: the inner mental life of a character or work as revealed in art and literature
senses.definitionCN: 艺术与文学中所揭示的人物或作品的内心生活
senses.example: The novel's psychology is revealed through small gestures, not speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的心理是通过细小动作而非言谈揭示的。
senses.why: Critics borrowed the discipline's name for what a text shows of the mind. The psychology of a character is the mind the writer has built, studied as if from outside.
senses.whyCN: 评论家借用了学科名，指文本所展示的心灵。人物的 psychology 就是作者建造的那颗心，像从外部一样被研究。

intro.en: Psychology starts as the study of the soul, not the brain. Greek psykhē 'breath, spirit' plus -logia 'study of' produced a Modern Latin coinage of the 16c.; English took it in the 1650s, and the object shifted from soul to mind to measurable behavior.
intro.cn: psychology 起初研究的是灵魂，不是大脑。希腊语 psykhē“呼吸、精神”加 -logia“对……的研究”造出一个 16 世纪的新拉丁语词；英语在 17 世纪 50 年代借入，研究对象从灵魂转到心智，再转到可测量的行为。

items.en: Psykhē meant 'breath, spirit, soul, life', probably akin to psykhein 'to blow, breathe'. The deeper PIE *bhes- 'to blow' is a reconstruction with no written record, so that layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: psykhē 意为“呼吸、精神、灵魂、生命”，可能与 psykhein“吹、呼吸”同源。更深的印欧语 *bhes-“吹”是没有书面记录的重构，因此该层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: -Logia 'study of' comes from logos 'word, reason, account'. A psychology is literally an account of the soul.
items.cn: -logia“对……的研究”来自 logos“言词、理性、论述”。一门 psychology 字面上就是“关于灵魂的论述”。

items.en: Psychologia was probably coined in Germany in the mid-16c., attributed to Melanchthon. It joined the Latinized Greek psykhē to -logia.
items.cn: psychologia 很可能是 16 世纪中在德国造出的，常归于梅兰希顿。它把拉丁化的希腊语 psykhē 与 -logia 结合。

items.en: The word enters English as 'the study of the soul'. The soul, not behavior, is the first object of the new discipline.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时意为“对灵魂的研究”。新学科最初的对象是灵魂，而不是行为。

items.en: The meaning 'science or study of the phenomena of the mind' is attested by 1748, in reference to Christian Wolff's Psychologia empirica (1732).
items.cn: “研究心理现象的科学”这一义项于 1748 年出现，指的是克里斯蒂安·沃尔夫的《经验心理学》（1732）。

items.en: The modern behavioral-sciences sense dates from the early 1890s, when laboratories and statistics redefined what counted as the mind's evidence.
items.cn: 现代行为科学义可追溯到 19 世纪 90 年代初，那时实验室与统计重新定义了什么才算心灵的证据。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the psych- or -ology shape but belongs to different roots; the meaning group shares the study or the mind itself.
note.cn: 形近组共享 psych- 或 -ology 的外形，但属于不同词根；近义组共享“研究”或“心灵本身”。

entries.definition: the branch of medicine that treats mental illness. It shares psych- but ends in 'healing', not 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗精神疾病的医学分支。它共享 psych-，但词尾是“治疗”而非“研究”。

entries.definition: the study of how living bodies work. It looks like psychology but its root is physis 'nature'.
entries.definitionCN: 生理学；研究活体如何运作。它形似 psychology，但词根是 physis“自然”。

entries.definition: a personality disorder marked by lack of empathy. It shares psych- but ends in 'suffering'.
entries.definitionCN: 以缺乏共情为特征的人格障碍。它共享 psych-，但词尾是“痛苦”。

entries.definition: a person who studies the mind. It is the same word plus the agent suffix -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学家。它是同一个词加上施事后缀 -ist。

entries.definition: the medical specialty that diagnoses and treats mental illness. It is clinical where psychology is academic.
entries.definitionCN: 诊断与治疗精神疾病的医学专科。它偏临床，而 psychology 偏学术。

entries.definition: the seat of thought, feeling and memory. It is the thing psychology studies, not the study.
entries.definitionCN: 思想、情感与记忆的所在。它是心理学研究的对象，而不是研究本身。

entries.definition: a person's or group's characteristic way of thinking. It matches the 'psychology of X' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体特有的思维方式。它对应“X 的 psychology”这一义项。

entries.definition: the therapeutic method founded by Freud for exploring the unconscious. It is one school within psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 弗洛伊德创立、用于探索无意识的治疗方法。它是心理学内部的一个学派。

entries.definition: observable action and conduct. It is the evidence that modern psychology prefers to the soul.
entries.definitionCN: 可观察的行动与举止。它是现代心理学取代灵魂之后所偏好的证据。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek psykhē 'soul, breath', the -logia 'study' ending, and the modern split into psychiatry and psychoanalysis.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 psykhē“灵魂、呼吸”、-logia“研究”词尾，以及现代分出的 psychiatry 与 psychoanalysis。

normal.en: psychology = psyche 'soul' + -logy 'study': first the soul, later the mind.
normal.cn: psychology = psyche“灵魂”+ -logy“研究”：先研究灵魂，后研究心智。

normal.en: Psyche was also the Greek girl loved by Eros, often drawn with butterfly wings — a soul with wings.
normal.cn: Psyche 还是希腊神话中被厄洛斯所爱的少女，常被画上蝶翼——一个长了翅膀的灵魂。

normal.en: Psychiatry treats the sick mind; psychology studies the mind in general. Same psyche, different second half.
normal.cn: psychiatry 治疗生病的心智；psychology 研究一般的心智。同一个 psyche，后半截不同。

normal.en: A psychologist is a psychologist; a psychiatrist is a doctor. The -ist and the -iatrist tell you.
normal.cn: psychologist 是心理学家；psychiatrist 是精神科医生。-ist 与 -iatrist 告诉你区别。

normal.en: Reverse psychology works because knowing the mind is already half of controlling it.
normal.cn: 反向心理之所以有效，是因为了解心智已经是控制它的一半。

abstract.en: The word is a mirror: it names both the study and the thing studied.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一面镜子：它既命名研究，也命名被研究之物。

abstract.en: It travels inward: from soul, to mind, to behavior, to the mind of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 它一路向内：从灵魂，到心智，到行为，再到人群的心。

abstract.en: Psychology is breath made legible: something invisible, turned into something you can describe.
abstract.cn: 心理学是把呼吸变得可读：某种看不见的东西，被转写成可以描述的东西。

examples.en: He took a course in psychology and started noticing his own habits.
examples.cn: 他上了一门心理学课程，开始注意到自己的习惯。

examples.en: The marketing team studies the psychology of impulse buying.
examples.cn: 营销团队研究冲动购物的心理。

examples.en: Using reverse psychology on a stubborn child often backfires.
examples.cn: 对固执的孩子使用反向心理，常常适得其反。

dict_mnemonic.text: psycho（心理）+ logy（学科）——研究心理的学问；谐音“赛可乐鸡”：赛前（psy）喝可乐（cho）吃鸡，琢磨对手心里想什么 → psychology 心理学；心理

root: 源自希腊语 psykhē“呼吸、灵魂、心灵”加 -logia“对……的研究”，经新拉丁语 psychologia 进入英语；核心是“对那口看不见的气息——灵魂与心智——的探究”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses around one object: the invisible mind. The word begins as the study of the soul, becomes the science of mental phenomena, then the mind of a person or crowd, a school of theory, a practical trick, a wartime weapon, and finally the inner life a novel reveals.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个对象：看不见的心智。这个词从“研究灵魂”开始，变成“研究心理现象的科学”，再指个人或群体的心理、一个理论学派、一种实用手段、一件战时武器，最后指小说所揭示的内心生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaning inward to listen to the breath-like mind and describe what it is doing.
core.cn: 核心意象：向内俯身，倾听那口气息般的心智，并描述它在做什么。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: its birth as soul-study, its 1748 mind-science, and its 1890s behavioral form.
branches.cn: 学科：作为灵魂研究的诞生、1748 年的心理科学，以及 1890 年代的行为科学形态。

branches.en: THE MIND ITSELF: a person's makeup, a group's inner life, and a character's inner life in art.
branches.cn: 心智本身：个人的心理构成、群体的内心生活，以及艺术中人物的内心。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: one theory-system among many, each with its own model of the mind.
branches.cn: 学派：众多理论体系中的一支，每一支都有自己的心灵模型。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL TRICK: reading and steering a person in the moment.
branches.cn: 实用手段：当场读懂并引导一个人。

branches.en: THE WEAPON: psychology applied to morale, as psychological warfare.
branches.cn: 武器：作用于士气的心理学，即心理战。

intro.en: Psychology is psych- plus -ology. Its family shows the Greek root psych- 'soul, mind' and the suffix -logy 'study', plus the related endings -ologist, -ological and -iatry.
intro.cn: psychology 是 psych- 加 -ology。它的词族展示希腊词根 psych-“灵魂、心智”与后缀 -logy“研究”，以及相关词尾 -ologist、-ological、-iatry。

latinIntro.en: Greek psykhē 'soul, breath' is the base of psyche, psychology and psychiatry; Greek logos 'word, reason' supplies -logy, -logical and -logue.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 psykhē“灵魂、呼吸”是 psyche、psychology、psychiatry 的基础；希腊语 logos“言词、理性”提供 -logy、-logical、-logue。

items.example: Psychology explains why we forget names so easily.
items.exampleCN: 心理学解释了为什么我们那么容易忘记名字。

items.example: The poem explores the wounded psyche of a soldier.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗探索一名士兵受伤的心灵。

items.meaning: the medical treatment of mental illness
items.example: She trained in psychiatry before opening a clinic.
items.exampleCN: 她在开设诊所前接受了精神病学训练。

items.meaning: the Freudian method of exploring the unconscious
items.example: Psychoanalysis asks what a dream hides.
items.exampleCN: 精神分析追问一个梦隐藏了什么。

items.example: The school hired a psychologist for its students.
items.exampleCN: 学校为学生聘请了一位心理学家。

items.meaning: of the mind or of psychology
items.example: The injury was psychological rather than physical.
items.exampleCN: 这处伤是心理上的，而非身体上的。

items.meaning: a person with a severe personality disorder
items.example: The character is written as a charming psychopath.
items.exampleCN: 这个角色被写成一个有魅力的精神变态者。

items.meaning: having bodily symptoms caused by the mind
items.meaningCN: 心身性的（心智影响身体）
items.exampleCN: 压力可以引起心身性头痛。

items.meaning: the study of phenomena outside orthodox psychology
items.meaningCN: 超心理学（正统心理学之外）
items.exampleCN: 超心理学研究传心术与千里眼。

items.example: The album's psychedelic colours swirl on screen.
items.exampleCN: 专辑的致幻色彩在屏幕上旋转。

definition_zh: 酒馆；酒吧；（澳新）旅店
definition_en: a building or room where alcoholic drinks are served and drunk, especially in Britain; also, in Australia and New Zealand, a hotel with a bar
core_image: 傍晚街角亮起暖灯的小店，木门一推开就是碰杯声
scene: 下班铃响过，几个人把工具袋往肩上一搭，拐进街角那家挂着旧木牌的小店。After the shift, the crew walked down to the pub on the corner for a quick drink.
sceneCN: 这里 pub 是「酒馆」（第 1 个义项：英国供人坐下喝酒的场所）；句意为下工之后，工人们走到街角那家酒馆喝一杯。图中可辨识物件：旧木牌、暖灯、吧台。

pos.zh: 酒馆；酒吧；（澳新）旅店

derivatives.zh: 与 public 同源、经营酒馆的人；英式英语指酒馆老板，拉丁语原义是包税人
pub 与 crawl 复合，指一晚连喝好几家酒馆
pub 加表示「常去者」的 -goer，指常泡酒馆的人

senses.title: A place where alcoholic drinks are served
senses.definition: a building or room, especially in Britain, where people sit and buy alcoholic drinks to drink there
senses.definitionCN: 尤指英国的建筑或房间，人们坐在里面买酒并当场饮用
senses.example: We met in a quiet pub behind the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站后面一家安静的酒馆碰了头。
senses.why: Pub is public house cut short, and a public house was simply a house open to the public for drink, so the short form still names a room anyone may walk into.
senses.whyCN: pub 是 public house（向公众开放的房子）的截短，而 public house 本就是指「对公众开放、可以进去喝酒的房子」，所以短词仍指谁都能推门进去的那间屋子。

senses.title: A hotel with a bar in Australia and New Zealand
senses.definition: in Australia and New Zealand, a hotel that has a bar and often also serves meals and lets rooms
senses.definitionCN: 在澳大利亚与新西兰，指带酒吧的旅店，常兼供饭食并出租房间
senses.example: They stayed two nights at the pub beside the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在公路边那家旅店住了两晚。
senses.why: On the long colonial roads one building sold drink, cooked meals and let a bed, so the word for the drinking room widened to cover the whole hotel.
senses.whyCN: 在漫长的殖民时期公路边，一栋房子同时卖酒、做饭、租床位，于是原本指饮酒房间的词扩大到了整间旅店。

senses.title: The local pub as a neighbourhood meeting place
senses.definition: the nearby pub understood as a regular social centre where neighbours meet and exchange news
senses.definitionCN: 把附近那家酒馆看作固定聚点，邻居在那里见面、交换消息
senses.example: The village pub is where everyone hears the news first.
senses.exampleCN: 村里那家酒馆是所有人最先听到消息的地方。
senses.why: The same room serves the same street every evening, so a business turns into the place where a neighbourhood talks, and English lets the old word carry that role too.
senses.whyCN: 同一间屋子每晚招待同一条街的人，一门生意便变成了街坊说话的地方，英语让这个旧词一并承担这重角色。

senses.title: Of or happening in a pub, used before a noun
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean served, held, or happening in a pub
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，表示「酒馆供应的、酒馆里举办的」
senses.example: Sunday pub lunches are a habit in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 周日去酒馆吃午饭是这个镇上的习惯。
senses.why: Once pub names a place, it can stand in front of another noun and mark that thing as belonging to the place, which is exactly how pub food and pub quizzes are formed.
senses.whyCN: pub 一旦指某个场所，就能站到另一个名词前面，标明那样东西属于这个场所，pub food 与 pub quiz 正是这样构成的。

intro.en: Pub is not inherited from Latin but clipped from the English phrase public house in the nineteenth century; the public part of that phrase goes back to Latin publicus, from populus, the people.
intro.cn: pub 并非直接从拉丁语继承而来，而是十九世纪从英语短语 public house 截短而成；其中 public 可上溯到拉丁语 publicus，而 publicus 又来自 populus（人民）。

items.en: Populus meant the people taken as one body, and it is the root behind the adjective publicus.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是形容词 publicus 背后的词根。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state, that is, open to all citizens rather than held privately.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」，也就是向全体公民开放、而非私人占有。

items.en: From the later seventeenth century English called an inn or tavern a public house, a house open to the public for eating and drinking.
items.cn: 十七世纪后期起，英语把客栈、酒馆称作 public house，即向公众开放、供人饮食的房子。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, first in British working speech, the phrase was cut down to the single syllable pub, and the short form spread quickly.
items.cn: 十九世纪，先是英国劳工阶层口语把这个短语截成单音节 pub，短形式很快传开。

items.en: Modern English uses pub for the British drinking place, for the Australian hotel, and inside compounds such as pub quiz, pub food and pub-crawl.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pub 指英国的饮酒场所、澳新的旅店，也用在 pub quiz、pub food、pub-crawl 这类复合词里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the phrase pub was cut from and its Latin relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other words for places that sell drink.
note.cn: 形近组收 pub 被截短之前的短语与它的拉丁同族词；近义组收其他表示卖酒场所的词。

entries.definition: The full form that pub was cut from: a house open to the public for food and drink.
entries.definitionCN: pub 被截短之前的完整形式：向公众开放、供饮食的房子。

entries.definition: In British English the keeper of a pub; the Latin word once meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中指酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原本指包税人。

entries.definition: Open to all people, or the people as a whole; the adjective inside public house.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众；public house 里用的正是这个形容词。

entries.definition: To make a text available to the public; built on the same Latin family as public.
entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行；与 public 同出一个拉丁词族。

entries.definition: A counter or room where drinks are served and drunk.
entries.definitionCN: 供应并供人饮用酒水的柜台或房间。

entries.definition: An old word for a place that sells drink and often food.
entries.definitionCN: 指卖酒、常兼供食物的旧词。

entries.definition: A small hotel that also serves meals and drink.
entries.definitionCN: 兼供饭食与酒水的小旅店。

entries.definition: A bar, especially in the old American West.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指美国旧西部的酒吧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a three-word phrase squeezed into one syllable, and behind that phrase stands a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个三词短语压成了一个音节，而短语背后是一个表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词。

normal.en: Pub is public house cut short: the endings fall away and two words become one syllable.
normal.cn: pub 是 public house 的截短：词尾脱落，两个词压缩成一个音节。

normal.en: The public in public house is Latin publicus, from populus, the people, so a pub was a house open to the people.
normal.cn: public house 里的 public 来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 出自 populus（人民），所以 pub 原本就是对人民开放的房子。

normal.en: A publican runs the pub, although the same Latin word once meant a tax collector, a very different trade.
normal.cn: publican 是经营酒馆的人，尽管同一个拉丁词从前指收税的人，两者行当大不相同。

normal.en: Pub quiz and pub lunch keep pub in front of a noun, marking something that happens inside that place.
normal.cn: pub quiz 与 pub lunch 把 pub 放在名词前，标明那件事就发生在这个场所里。

normal.en: In Australia and New Zealand one word covers the bar and the bedrooms, because one building once did both jobs.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚与新西兰，一个词同时覆盖酒吧与客房，因为从前一栋房子就兼做这两件事。

abstract.en: The word is a door swinging open on a warm evening, with strangers sitting close enough to talk.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一扇在暖夜里推开的门，里面的陌生人坐得近到可以交谈。

abstract.en: Cutting a long phrase down to one beat is how a language makes room for the thing people do most often.
abstract.cn: 把一个长短语砍成一个节拍，是语言在为人们最常做的事腾出位置。

abstract.en: A pub sells drink, but people come back for the same three chairs and the same familiar noise.
abstract.cn: 酒馆卖的是酒，可人们回来找的是同样那三把椅子和同样熟悉的喧闹。

examples.en: We had lunch at a pub by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边一家酒馆吃了午饭。

examples.en: The pub closes at eleven on weekdays.
examples.cn: 这家酒馆工作日十一点关门。

examples.en: He now runs the pub his grandfather opened.
examples.cn: 他现在经营着祖父当年开的那家酒馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布」——推门进去，帕布一声放下杯子，就是街角那家酒馆。

root: pub 是英语短语 public house（向公众开放的房子）在十九世纪的截短形式；public 出自拉丁语 publicus，publicus 又来自 populus（人民）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a house open to the public for drink; the senses divide into the British drinking room, the Australian hotel, the role of neighbourhood centre, and the attributive use before another noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「向公众开放、可供饮酒的房子」；义项由此分出英式饮酒场所、澳新旅店、街坊聚点的角色，以及放在名词前的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner doorway with a warm lamp above it, swinging open on a room full of talk.

senses.title: Available for everyone to use
senses.definition: provided for all people to use, rather than for one person or a small group
senses.definitionCN: 供所有人使用，而不是供某个人或某个小圈子使用
senses.example: The public library stays open until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公共图书馆开到晚上九点。
senses.why: The Latin adjective named what belonged to the people as a body, so a thing held in common rather than privately was called public.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本指「属于人民全体的」，因此凡由众人共有、不由私人占有的东西，就被称作 public。

senses.title: Known or seen by everyone
senses.definition: known or seen by everyone, with nothing kept secret
senses.definitionCN: 所有人都知道或看见的，没有任何部分被保密
senses.example: The report became public after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判结束后，这份报告被公开了。
senses.why: If something belongs to all the people, hiding it from them makes no sense, so shared ownership slides into shared knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然属于全体人民，瞒着他们就没有道理，于是「共有」自然滑向「共知」。

senses.title: Relating to the people or the state
senses.definition: relating to the people as a whole, or to work done by the state on their behalf
senses.definitionCN: 与全体人民有关，或与以人民名义运作的国家事务有关
senses.example: Public spending on roads fell last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年用于道路的公共开支下降了。
senses.why: Money and decisions that concern everyone are handled in the name of all, so the adjective also marks what the state holds rather than what a private owner holds.
senses.whyCN: 涉及所有人的钱和决定都以全体之名来打理，所以这个词也用来标明由国家、而非私人掌握的事物。

senses.title: The people as a whole
senses.definition: the people of a country or community considered as one body, especially as readers, viewers or voters
senses.definitionCN: 把一个国家或社区的人看作一个整体，尤指读者、观众或选民
senses.example: The gallery opened its doors to the public at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆十点向公众开门。
senses.why: The adjective was used so often with a noun left unsaid that it became a noun itself, naming the crowd a place is open to.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常与一个被省略的名词连用，久而久之自己变成了名词，专指场所向其开放的那群人。

senses.title: An open setting where others can see and hear
senses.definition: an open place or setting where other people can see and hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 一个开放的场景，别人能看见、听见发生的事
senses.example: She has never sung in public before.
senses.exampleCN: 她以前从未在公开场合唱过歌。
senses.why: A public place is one open to all, so the noun in the phrase in public names that open setting itself, in contrast with a private room.
senses.whyCN: public 的地方就是对所有人开放的地方，因此 in public 中的名词正指这个开放场景本身，与私密房间相对。

intro.en: Public came into English through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people; the noun use is a later English development.
intro.cn: public 经法语从拉丁语 publicus 进入英语，publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词；名词用法是英语后来发展出来的。

items.en: Populus meant the people as a body, and it is the base from which publicus was formed.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是构成 publicus 的基础。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state; an older form poplicus is recorded, which shows the link with populus.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」；文献中还有更早的形式 poplicus，可见它与 populus 的联系。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as public with the same sense of open and common, and passed it into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 public，保留「开放的、共有的」意思，十五世纪传入英语。

items.en: English began using public as a noun for the people, first in phrases such as in public and then standing alone with the definite article.
items.cn: 英语开始把 public 用作指人民的名词，先出现在 in public 这类短语中，后来能单独与定冠词连用。

items.en: Modern English builds public transport, public health and public opinion, and pairs public with private as opposite poles.
items.cn: 现代英语构成 public transport、public health、public opinion 等说法，并把 public 与 private 配成对立的两极。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is shared or open.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁词干上的英语词；近义组收表示「共有、开放」的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行，出自拉丁语 publicare。

entries.definitionCN: 元首经选举产生的国家，出自拉丁语 res publica（公共之事）。

entries.definition: A British pub keeper; the Latin word meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英国的酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原指包税人。

entries.definition: Shared by a group rather than owned by one person.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共用，而非一人独占的。

entries.definition: Done or held by all the members of a group together.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体全体成员共同做出或持有的。

entries.definition: Not closed or hidden, and free for anyone to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 未关闭、未隐藏，任何人都可进入的。

entries.definition: Relating to a town and the duties of the people who live there.
entries.definitionCN: 与城镇及居民义务有关的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people, and English later let it stand alone as a noun for those people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词，英语后来让它单独作名词，指那些人民。

normal.en: Public came through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people.
normal.cn: public 经法语来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词。

normal.en: The noun public is the adjective standing alone, naming the people a place is open to.
normal.cn: 名词 public 就是单独站立的形容词，指场所向其开放的那群人。

normal.en: Public and private form a pair: one belongs to all, the other belongs to one person or one household.
normal.cn: public 与 private 成对：前者属于所有人，后者属于一个人或一个家庭。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity and publicly is public with -ly, and both keep the same idea of openness.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，publicly 是 public 加 -ly，两者都保留着同一层「开放」的意思。

normal.en: Publish comes from Latin publicare, to make public, which is why publishing is always an act aimed at readers.
normal.cn: publish 出自拉丁 publicare（使公开），所以出版始终是朝着读者做出的动作。

abstract.en: The word is a lamp in the middle of a square: no side of the square is darker than another.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是广场中央的一盏灯：广场的任何一边都不会比另一边更暗。

abstract.en: A matter turns public when the cost of hiding it grows higher than the cost of showing it.
abstract.cn: 一件事之所以转为公开，往往是因为隐瞒的代价高过了示人的代价。

abstract.en: English keeps one word for shared ownership, shared knowledge and shared space, as if all three were one openness.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个词涵盖共有、共知与共用空间，仿佛这三者本就是同一种开放。

examples.en: The park is public land, so anyone may walk there.
examples.cn: 这座公园是公共土地，任何人都可以进去散步。

examples.en: Details of the deal were made public yesterday.
examples.cn: 交易的细节昨天被公开了。

examples.en: He rarely speaks in public.
examples.cn: 他很少在公开场合讲话。

senses.title: Putting a book into the world
senses.titleCN: 出版：把一本书推进世界
senses.definition: the act of producing a book, magazine, or other work and offering it to the public
senses.definitionCN: 制作书籍、杂志或其他作品并向公众提供的行为
senses.example: The publication of her memoir took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她回忆录的出版花了两年时间。
senses.why: The sense 'issuing of a written or printed work to the public by sale or distribution' is recorded from the 1570s. The older 'making known' turns into a physical process: print, bind, sell.
senses.whyCN: “通过销售或分发向公众发行文字或印刷作品”这一义项记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。更早的“使人知晓”变成了物理过程：印刷、装订、销售。

senses.title: The thing issued: a publication
senses.titleCN: 出版物：被推出去的那件东西
senses.definition: a book, journal, or other work that has been published
senses.definitionCN: 已出版的书籍、期刊或其他作品
senses.example: The library subscribes to several scientific publications.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆订阅了几种科学出版物。
senses.why: From the 1650s the word also names the thing issued and offered. The noun of action becomes a countable object — the deed and its product share one form.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 50 年代起，这个词也命名被发行、被提供的那个东西。动作名词变成了可数物体——行为与产物共用同一个形式。

senses.title: Making research public
senses.titleCN: 发表：把研究交到同行手里
senses.definition: the act of making research, writing, or an article available to the public, especially in a journal
senses.definitionCN: 使研究、文字或文章为公众可得的行为，尤指在期刊上
senses.example: Publication in a peer-reviewed journal is required for promotion.
senses.exampleCN: 在同行评审期刊上发表是晋升的必要条件。
senses.why: Academic life narrowed the 1570s issuing sense to the author's act: a paper is 'published' when it enters the public record. Publication becomes the currency of a career.
senses.whyCN: 学术生活把 16 世纪 70 年代的发行义收窄为作者的行为：论文进入公共记录即“发表”。publication 于是成了学术生涯的通货。

senses.title: Making it known: the original sense
senses.titleCN: 公布、公开宣布：最初的那个意思
senses.definition: the act of making something publicly known; official notification to the people at large
senses.definitionCN: 使某事为公众所知的行为；向大众的官方通告
senses.example: The publication of the findings surprised the whole industry.
senses.exampleCN: 研究结果的公布震动了整个行业。
senses.why: Late 14c. publicacioun meant 'the act of making publicly known, notification to the people at large'. Before print, publication was simply speech made public.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪后期的 publicacioun 意为“使公众知晓的行为、向大众通告”。在印刷术之前，publication 只是把话公开说出来。

senses.title: The release of an edition
senses.titleCN: 发行、发售：某一版次被放出去
senses.definition: the release of a particular edition or issue for sale or distribution
senses.definitionCN: 某一版本或期次为销售或分发而发行
senses.example: The publication of the new edition was timed for the holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 新版的发行被安排在假期。
senses.why: Once publication is an event in the market, it can be scheduled, delayed, and dated. The abstract act becomes a release date on a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 publication 成为市场中的事件，它就可以被排期、推迟、标注日期。抽象的行为变成了日历上的发行日。

senses.title: A periodical you can hold
senses.titleCN: 刊物：按期出的一本东西
senses.definition: a periodical, such as a magazine or journal, issued at regular intervals
senses.definitionCN: 定期发行的期刊，如杂志或学报
senses.example: She writes a column for a trade publication.
senses.exampleCN: 她为一家行业刊物撰写专栏。
senses.why: The object sense specializes: a publication is not any book but one of a series that keeps appearing. The issue is the unit, the publication is the title.
senses.whyCN: 物体义发生专门化：publication 不是任意一本书，而是持续出现的一系列中的一种。一期是单位，publication 是刊名。

senses.title: Exposing private material
senses.titleCN: 披露、公开：把私下的东西摊到阳光下
senses.definition: the act of making private letters, records, or images open to public view
senses.definitionCN: 使私人信件、记录或影像向公众开放的行为
senses.example: The publication of the private letters caused a scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 这些私人信件的公开引发了一场丑闻。
senses.why: The original 'making known' sense survives strongly when the material was never meant to be known. Publication here is exposure, not commerce.
senses.whyCN: 当材料本不该被知道时，最初的“使人知晓”义就强烈地存活着。这里的 publication 是曝光，而不是买卖。

senses.title: Publication in media law
senses.titleCN: 法律上的传播、发表：让第三方看到
senses.definition: in media law, the communication of defamatory or protected material to a third party
senses.definitionCN: 媒体法中，向第三方传播诽谤性或受保护材料的行为
senses.example: The court asked whether the email amounted to publication.
senses.exampleCN: 法院要判断这封电子邮件是否构成“传播”。
senses.why: Law needs a precise moment when words leave private hands. 'Publication' supplies it: any communication to a third party, even one reader, can be publication.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个精确的时刻，判定言语何时离开私人之手。publication 提供了它：向第三方——哪怕只有一位读者——的任何传达都可构成“传播”。

senses.title: The publishing trade
senses.titleCN: 出版业、出版工作：这一行的总称
senses.definition: the business or activity of publishing as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 作为职业的出版业务或活动
senses.example: She has worked in publication for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在出版行业工作了二十年。
senses.why: The noun of action can name an entire trade, just as 'education' names a field. What began as one act of making public becomes an industry.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词可以命名整个行业，正如 education 命名一个领域。最初“使公开”的一个动作，变成了一个产业。

intro.en: Publication is from Latin publicare 'make public', built on publicus 'of the people'. It begins as the act of telling everyone, gains the printing sense in the 1570s, and then splits into the act, the object, the edition, and the law.
intro.cn: publication 来自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，其基础是 publicus“属于人民的”。它起初指“告诉所有人”的行为，16 世纪 70 年代获得印刷义，随后分裂为行为、物体、版次与法律义。

items.en: Publicare meant 'to make public', from publicus 'of the people, common'. Publicus was altered from Old Latin poplicus, from populus 'people'; the deeper origin of populus is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: publicare 意为“使公开”，来自 publicus“属于人民的、公共的”。publicus 由古拉丁语 poplicus 变来，后者来自 populus“人民”；populus 更深的来源不确定，标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Publicatio meant 'a making public', also 'an adjudging to the public treasury'. The legal sense of handing something to the state runs beside the sense of announcing.
items.cn: publicatio 意为“使公开”，也指“判归国库”。把某物交给国家的法律义，与“宣布”的义项并行。

items.en: Publicacioun enters English as 'the act of making publicly known, notification to the people at large'. Print does not exist yet; publication is an act of speech and notice.
items.cn: publicacioun 进入英语时意为“使公众知晓的行为、向大众通告”。印刷术尚未出现；publication 是一种言说与公告的行为。

items.en: The meaning 'the issuing of a written or printed work to the public by sale or distribution' is recorded by the 1570s. The printing press gives the word a product.
items.cn: “通过销售或分发向公众发行文字或印刷作品”这一义项记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。印刷机给了这个词一个产品。

items.en: From the 1650s the word also names the thing so issued and offered. Act and object now share one noun.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪 50 年代起，这个词也命名被发行、被提供的那个东西。行为与物体如今共用一个名词。

items.en: Academic publication becomes a career measure, periodicals multiply, and media law fixes 'communication to a third party' as publication. The old 'making known' sense survives in every one.
items.cn: 学术发表成为职业衡量标准，期刊大量增加，媒体法把“向第三方传达”确定为 publication。古老的“使人知晓”义在每一个新义里都存活下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the publ- opening or the -ation ending but differs in meaning; the near group names the act, the object, and the audience.
note.cn: 形近组共享 publ- 开头或 -ation 结尾，但意义不同；近义组则分别命名行为、物体与受众。

entries.definition: attention given to someone by the media. It ends in -ity and names attention, not an issued work.
entries.definitionCN: 媒体给予的公众关注。它以 -ity 结尾，指注意力，而不是被发行的作品。

entries.definition: the act of publicizing something. It looks like publication but its ending is -ization, not -ation.
entries.definitionCN: 宣传、使公开的行为。它形似 publication，但词尾是 -ization 而非 -ation。

entries.definition: the act of publishing something again. The prefix re- marks a second issuing.
entries.definitionCN: 再出版；重新发表。前缀 re- 标记第二次发行。

entries.definition: a tavern keeper or, in older use, a tax collector. It shares the publi- opening but ends in -an, not -ation.
entries.definitionCN: 酒馆老板，旧时也指收税人。它共享 publi- 开头，但词尾是 -an 而非 -ation。

entries.definition: the business of producing books and periodicals. It names the trade, where publication can name a single act or object.
entries.definitionCN: 图书与期刊的生产行业。它命名行业，而 publication 可指单次行为或单个物体。

entries.definition: a particular edition or number of a periodical, or the act of releasing it.
entries.definitionCN: 期刊的某一版次或期号，或发行它的行为。

entries.definition: the act of making a film, record, or statement available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 使电影、唱片或声明向公众可得的行为。

entries.definition: a public statement that informs people of something. It matches publication's original sense.
entries.definitionCN: 告知公众某事的公开声明。它对应 publication 的本义。

entries.definition: the number of copies of a publication sold or distributed.
entries.definitionCN: 出版物售出或分发的份数。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin publicus 'of the people', publicare 'make public', and the 1570s printing sense that turned an announcement into an object.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”、publicare“使公开”，以及 16 世纪 70 年代把公告变成物品的印刷义。

normal.en: publication = public + -ation: the act of making something public.
normal.cn: publication = public + -ation：使某物公开的行为。

normal.en: publicare 'make public' is the same verb behind publish: publication is the noun of that act.
normal.cn: publicare“使公开”也是 publish 背后的动词：publication 就是那个动作的名词。

normal.en: Before print, publication was a voice in the square; after print, it is a book on a shelf.
normal.cn: 印刷术之前，publication 是广场上的一个声音；印刷术之后，它是书架上的一本书。

normal.en: A publication can be both the deed and the thing: 'the publication of the book' and 'a scientific publication'.
normal.cn: publication 既可以是行为也可以是东西：“这本书的出版”和“一份科学出版物”。

normal.en: In law, publication needs only a third pair of eyes — even one reader can count.
normal.cn: 在法律上，publication 只需要第三双眼睛——哪怕只有一位读者也算。

abstract.en: The core is a door opened: what was private becomes available to all.
abstract.cn: 核心是一扇被打开的门：原本私下的东西变成人人可得。

abstract.en: One act, three products: knowledge, a printed object, and an industry.
abstract.cn: 一个动作，三种产物：知识、一件印刷品、一个产业。

abstract.en: The word keeps its original promise: publication is first of all making known.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终守着最初的承诺：publication 首先是使人知晓。

examples.en: The publication of the report was delayed by legal review.
examples.cn: 报告的公布因法律审查而推迟。

examples.en: She lists three publications on her academic CV.
examples.cn: 她在学术简历上列了三项出版物。

examples.en: The newspaper is a daily publication with a large circulation.
examples.cn: 这份报纸是一份发行量很大的日报。

dict_mnemonic.text: public（公众）+ ation（行为）——把东西送到公众面前；谐音“帕布利凯申”：把稿子“扑”到印刷机上，公开（public）地发出去 → publication 出版；公布

root: 源自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，由 publicus“属于人民的”加动词后缀构成，名词 publicatio 经古法语进入英语；核心是“把原本私下的东西交给所有人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses on one movement: from private to public. The word begins as an announcement, becomes the printing and sale of a work, then the work itself, an edition, a periodical, an exposure, a legal communication, and finally an industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个动作：从私下到公开。这个词从“公告”开始，变成作品的印刷与销售，再指作品本身、一个版次、一种期刊、一次曝光、一次法律意义上的传达，最后指一个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a private manuscript pushed through the press and handed out to strangers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份私人手稿被送进印刷机，然后分发到陌生人手里。

branches.en: THE ACT OF ISSUING: producing a work, and releasing a particular edition.
branches.cn: 发行行为：制作一部作品，以及发行某个版次。

branches.en: THE THING ISSUED: a published work, and a periodical that keeps appearing.
branches.cn: 被发行之物：已出版的作品，以及持续出现的期刊。

branches.en: MAKING KNOWN: academic publication, and the original sense of public announcement.
branches.cn: 使人知晓：学术发表，以及公开宣告的本义。

branches.en: EXPOSURE: private material brought into the light, willing or not.
branches.cn: 曝光：私人材料被带到光下，无论当事人是否愿意。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC SPHERE: publication in media law, and publishing as a trade.
branches.cn: 公共领域：媒体法中的“传播”，以及作为行业的出版。

intro.en: Publication is publ- plus -ication. Its family shows Latin publicus 'of the people', the verb publicare, the noun ending -ation, and the agent and quality endings -er, -ist, -ity and -ize.
intro.cn: publication 是 publ- 加 -ication。它的词族展示拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”、动词 publicare、名词词尾 -ation，以及施事与性质词尾 -er、-ist、-ity、-ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin publicus 'of the people' is the base of public, publish and publication; publicare 'make public' yields publication and publication's verb publish, while -ity and -ize build publicity and publicize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”是 public、publish、publication 的基础；publicare“使公开”给出 publication 及其动词 publish，而 -ity 与 -ize 构成 publicity 与 publicize。

items.meaning: the act of making public; a published work
items.example: The publication of the atlas took ten years.
items.exampleCN: 这本图集的出版花了十年。

items.meaning: open to all; the people as a whole
items.example: The garden is open to the public.

items.meaning: to make public; to issue a work
items.example: They publish four issues a year.

items.meaning: a person or company that issues works
items.exampleCN: 出版商接受了她的手稿。

items.meaning: to bring something to public attention
items.example: The team publicized the event on social media.
items.exampleCN: 团队在社交媒体上宣传了这场活动。

items.meaning: the state of being known; media attention
items.exampleCN: 这场审判带来了不受欢迎的关注。
她的公关安排了三场采访。

items.example: The republication includes a new preface.
The draft is not yet publishable.

items.meaning: the stage before a work is published
items.exampleCN: 出版前的样书被送到了评论者手中。

definition_zh: 宣传；曝光度；公众关注；宣传材料
definition_en: the attention that a person or thing gets from the media and the public; the work of attracting such attention; material issued to promote something
core_image: 聚光灯打到舞台中央，台下无数镜头同时抬起来
scene: 新店开张前一周，街口的广告牌、手机推送和报纸角落都在说同一件事。The little bakery got more publicity from one photograph than from a year of advertising.
sceneCN: 这里 publicity 是「媒体关注、曝光度」（第 1 个义项：来自媒体与公众的注意）；句意为这家小面包店靠一张照片得到的关注，胜过一整年的广告。图中可辨识物件：广告牌、聚光灯、镜头。

pos.zh: 宣传；曝光度；公众关注；宣传材料

derivatives.zh: public 加动词后缀 -ize，义为「宣传；推广」
public 加表人后缀 -ist，义为「公关人员；宣传员」
去掉名词后缀 -ity 得到的形容词，义为「公共的；公开的」

senses.title: Attention from the media and the public
senses.definition: the attention that a person, product or event receives from newspapers, television and the public
senses.definitionCN: 人、产品、事件从报纸、电视和公众那里获得的注意
senses.example: The court case brought the family unwanted publicity.
senses.exampleCN: 这场官司给这家人带来了他们并不想要的关注。
senses.why: Publicity is the noun form of public, so it names the state of being seen by everyone; the media only make that state visible.
senses.whyCN: publicity 是 public 的名词形式，本指「被所有人看见的状态」，媒体只是把这种状态变得看得见。

senses.title: The work of attracting public attention
senses.definition: the business or activity of persuading the public to notice a product, a person or an event
senses.definitionCN: 设法让公众注意某个产品、人物或事件的工作
senses.example: She works in publicity for a film company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家电影公司做宣传工作。
senses.why: Once being seen has value, somebody must produce that visibility, so the noun also names the deliberate work of drawing eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「被看见」有了价值，就得有人去制造这种可见度，于是这个词也指刻意把目光引过来的工作。

senses.title: Material issued to promote something
senses.definition: printed or filmed material sent out to tell the public about something
senses.definitionCN: 为向公众介绍某事而发出的印刷品或影像材料
senses.example: The hotel sent publicity to every travel agent in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店给城里每一家旅行社都寄了宣传材料。
senses.why: The work of publicity produces sheets, pictures and short films, and the same noun can stand for the things it hands out.
senses.whyCN: 宣传工作会产出文稿、图片和短片，同一个名词也就能指它发出去的那些东西。

senses.title: The condition of being open to public knowledge
senses.titleCN: 公开性；为人所知的状态
senses.definition: the state of a matter being open to public knowledge rather than kept private
senses.definitionCN: 一件事向公众知识开放、而非被私下保留的状态
senses.example: The publicity of the hearing was itself part of the punishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这场听证的公开本身就是惩罚的一部分。
senses.why: Behind the media sense sits an older legal idea that a matter belongs to the public, and the noun can still name that openness on its own.
senses.whyCN: 媒体义项背后是更早的法律观念：一件事属于公众，这个名词至今仍能单指这种公开状态。

intro.en: Publicity is public plus the noun ending -ity, modelled on a medieval Latin noun and on French publicité; its first English sense was the state of being public, and the media sense came later.
intro.cn: publicity 是 public 加名词后缀 -ity，以中世纪拉丁名词与法语 publicité 为范本；英语最早的义项是「公开的状态」，媒体义项是后来才有的。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people, and from it Latin built nouns for the quality of being public.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民的」，拉丁语由它造出表示「公开性质」的名词。

items.en: Medieval Latin publicitas named the quality of being public, and it is generally thought to have supplied the model for the French and English forms.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 publicitas 指「公开的性质」；一般认为这个名词为法语和英语的形式提供了范本。

items.en: French publicité widened the sense to making something known to the public, and English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 publicité 把词义扩大到「使公众知晓某事」，英语在十八世纪借入这个词。

items.en: English publicity first meant the state of being public, then shifted to the business of drawing public attention as newspapers and advertising grew.
items.cn: 英语 publicity 先指「公开的状态」，随着报纸与广告的发展，转而指「吸引公众注意的行当」。

items.en: Modern English uses publicity for media attention, for the promotion industry, and for the sheets and clips that industry sends out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 publicity 指媒体关注、宣传行业，以及该行业发出的文稿与片段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for attention and for the work of getting it.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的形式；近义组收表示「关注」以及「争取关注的工作」的名词。

entries.definition: Open to all, or the people as a whole; the adjective behind publicity.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众；publicity 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something widely known on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意让某事广为人知。

entries.definition: A person paid to keep a name in the papers.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇让某个名字持续见报的人。

entries.definition: To issue a text for the public to read.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字发行出来供公众阅读。

entries.definition: Activity that helps sell or popularize something.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助销售或推广某事物的活动。

entries.definition: The state of being seen or discussed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人看到或谈论的状态。

entries.definition: Paid messages that persuade people to buy.
entries.definitionCN: 付费的、说服人们购买的信息。

entries.definition: Loud claims that inflate interest in something.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物的热度吹高的说法。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the adjective public with -ity attached, and both go back to the Latin quality of being open to the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是形容词 public 加上 -ity，两者都回到拉丁语「向人民开放」这一性质。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity, an ending that turns a quality into a noun, so it names the state of being public.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，这个后缀把性质变成名词，所以它指「处于公开状态」。

normal.en: The Latin model is publicitas, a medieval noun for exactly that quality.
normal.cn: 它的拉丁范本是 publicitas，一个正指这种性质的中世纪名词。

normal.en: Publicity and publicist share a stem: one is the attention, the other is the person paid to produce it.
normal.cn: publicity 与 publicist 同词干：前者是关注，后者是受雇制造关注的人。

normal.en: Publicize is the verb, and it means to make something public on purpose.
normal.cn: publicize 是对应的动词，意为有意把某事公开。

normal.en: A publicity stunt is a planned act whose only real purpose is to be reported.
normal.cn: publicity stunt 是一种安排好的举动，唯一真正的目的就是被报道。

abstract.en: The word is a spotlight switched on: before it, a thing merely exists; after it, everyone has an opinion.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一盏打开的聚光灯：亮之前东西只是存在，亮之后人人都有了看法。

abstract.en: Attention can be manufactured, not only received, which is why one noun covers the light and the people who aim it.
abstract.cn: 关注可以被制造，而不只是被接受，所以同一个名词既指那束光，也指操纵光的人。

abstract.en: When privacy is sold, publicity becomes a price, and the same word names the bill.
abstract.cn: 当隐私被拿去交换，曝光就成了一种价格，同一个词也用来指那张账单。

examples.en: The film got plenty of publicity before it opened.
examples.cn: 这部电影上映前就获得了大量宣传。

examples.en: He hired a firm to handle publicity for the tour.
examples.cn: 他请了一家公司为巡演做宣传。

examples.en: The case attracted publicity across the country.
examples.cn: 这起案件在全国范围内引起了关注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布利瑟提」——把东西摆到人人都看得见的灯下，就是 publicity，宣传与曝光。

root: 拉丁语 publicus（属于人民的）→ 中世纪拉丁 publicitas（公开的性质）→ 法语 publicité → 英语 publicity；由 public 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，核心是「被公众看见」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being open to the public eye; the senses divide into media attention, the work of attracting it, the material sent out, and the bare state of openness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「暴露在公众目光之下」；义项由此分为媒体关注、争取关注的工作、发出的材料，以及纯粹的公开状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight striking the middle of a stage while every camera below lifts at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯打在舞台中央，台下所有镜头同时抬起。

branches.en: one photograph reprinted in a hundred papers
branches.cn: 一张照片被上百家报纸转载

branches.en: a name repeated until strangers recognize it
branches.cn: 一个名字被重复到陌生人也能认出

branches.en: a desk of staff ringing editors all morning
branches.cn: 一整个上午给编辑打电话的办公桌

branches.en: an envelope of glossy sheets for travel agents
branches.cn: 寄给旅行社的一叠光面宣传页

branches.en: a hearing held with the doors left open
branches.cn: 大门敞开举行的听证

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin adjective for what belongs to the people and by the English noun ending -ity, which names a quality or state.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词和指性质、状态的名词后缀 -ity 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
